definition_zh: 植被；某一地区全部植物；（医学）赘生物
definition_en: the plant life of an area taken as a whole, especially what covers the ground; in medicine, an abnormal growth on a body surface
core_image: 一片土地被草木密密铺满，从贴地的苔藓一直连到高处的树冠，像一床会呼吸的绿被
scene: 沙丘表面只有薄薄一层草木；风一吹沙就移动，研究员靠记录这层草木的厚薄与种类判断沙丘是否稳定。Thin vegetation holds the dunes together against the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetation 指「一个地区地表全部植物形成的覆盖层」（第 1 个义项：把一地植物整体看待）；句意为稀疏的植被把沙丘粘在一起，抵御风的搬运。

pos.zh: 植被；某一地区的全部植物（不可数）
（医学）赘生物；心瓣膜或体表长出的异常组织

derivatives.zh: 生长；像植物一样过呆板生活
营养生长的；植物状态的

senses.title: Collective plant life of a region
senses.titleCN: 一个地区整体看待的植物
senses.definition: the whole body of plants growing in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物
senses.example: The vegetation of the island is mostly low scrub.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的植被以低矮灌丛为主。
senses.why: Vegetation is the noun of state built on vegetare 'to quicken, make lively': wherever plants take hold, the ground is made lively.
senses.whyCN: vegetation 是由表示「使有生气」的 vegetare 加名词后缀构成的状态名词：凡是植物扎下根的地方，土地就活了起来。

senses.title: The ground-covering layer
senses.titleCN: 贴地铺开、护住土壤的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of plants that covers the ground and protects the soil
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地表并保护土壤的植物层
senses.example: Thin vegetation holds the dunes together against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 稀疏的植被把沙丘粘在一起，抵御风。
senses.why: The collective sense narrows here to what touches the surface: roots bind grains, stems slow the wind, and the ground stops moving.
senses.whyCN: 整体义在此收窄为「接触地表」的部分：根抓住沙粒，茎挡住风，地面便不再移动。

senses.title: Rank or luxuriant growth
senses.titleCN: 长得过盛、几乎挡住路的草木
senses.definition: plants growing thickly and abundantly in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地长得繁茂浓密的植物
senses.example: Vegetation grew thick along the irrigation ditch.
senses.exampleCN: 灌渠边的草木长得又密又高。
senses.why: When growth runs ahead of use, the word shifts from what is there to how much of it there is, and the tone becomes almost a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 当生长超出需要，词义就从「有什么」转向「有多少」，语气也近乎抱怨。

senses.title: A plant community or type
senses.titleCN: 按形态划分的一类植物群落
senses.definition: a class of plant community distinguished by its structure and species
senses.definitionCN: 按结构与物种划分出的植物群落类型
senses.example: Botanists classify the valley's vegetation into four formations.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把谷地的植被分为四个群系。
senses.why: Modern ecology turns the mass noun into a countable technical term: each formation is a named package of species and structure.
senses.whyCN: 现代生态学把这个不可数名词变成可数的术语：每个群系都是物种与结构组成的有名组合。

senses.title: The record made by a survey
senses.titleCN: 调查后绘制出的植被记录
senses.definition: the plants of an area as recorded, mapped or described by a survey
senses.definitionCN: 经调查、绘图或描述记录下来的植被
senses.example: The team finished a vegetation survey before the dam was built.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝动工前，团队完成了植被调查。
senses.why: Surveying fixes the living layer into data, so the same word now names a map, a list and a baseline for later comparison.
senses.whyCN: 调查把这层活的东西固定成资料，同一个词于是既指图，也指清单，还指日后比对的基线。

senses.title: What is cleared away
senses.titleCN: 被当作障碍清理掉的草木
senses.definition: plants regarded as an obstacle and removed from a site
senses.definitionCN: 被视为障碍而从场地清除的植物
senses.example: Workers cleared the vegetation around the new pipeline.
senses.exampleCN: 工人清除了新管线周围的植被。
senses.why: Once plants are in the way of a project, the word stops describing an ecosystem and starts describing material to be removed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦草木挡了工程的路，这个词就不再描述生态系统，而开始指待清除的对象。

senses.title: Abnormal tissue growth
senses.titleCN: 体内长出的异常组织
senses.definition: a mass of abnormal tissue, especially on a heart valve or body surface
senses.definitionCN: 异常长出的组织块，尤指心瓣膜或体表上的
senses.example: Echocardiography showed a small vegetation on the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 超声心动图显示瓣膜上有一个小的赘生物。
senses.why: Medical Latin applied the plant-growth word to anything that sprouts where it should not, so the image of unwanted sprouting carries over.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语把这个「植物生长」的词用到一切不该长却长出来的东西上，杂草蔓生的意象因此延续。

senses.title: Plant cover read as a climate record
senses.titleCN: 被当作气候档案来读的植被
senses.definition: past plant cover reconstructed from pollen, seeds or other traces
senses.definitionCN: 从花粉、种子等遗迹重建出的过去植物覆盖
senses.example: Pollen in the lake mud records how the vegetation changed.
senses.exampleCN: 湖泥里的花粉记录了植被如何变化。
senses.why: Because plant cover answers to rainfall and temperature, its fossil traces become a thermometer for ancient climates.
senses.whyCN: 植物覆盖随降水与温度而变，因此它的化石遗迹成了测量古气候的温度计。

intro.en: Vegetation comes from Medieval Latin vegetatio 'a quickening, growth', from vegetare 'to enliven', built on vegetus 'lively'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vegetation 来自中世纪拉丁 vegetatio「使有生气、生长」，源于 vegetare「使有生气」，再往前是 vegetus「有活力的」。年代为约数。

items.en: Vegere meant 'to be lively, active'. Its deeper origin is not settled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: vegere 意为「有生气、活动着」。其更深来源没有定论，凡为它给出的印欧形式都是重构形式。

items.en: The participle vegetus 'lively, vigorous' supplied the adjective from which the verb was felt to come.
items.cn: 分词 vegetus「有活力的、精神抖擞的」提供了形容词，人们也觉得动词正是由它而来。

items.en: Vegetare 'to enliven, animate' produced Medieval Latin vegetatio 'a making lively, growth'.
items.cn: vegetare「使有生气、使活动」产生了中世纪拉丁 vegetatio「使有生气、生长」。

items.en: English adopted vegetation in the seventeenth century for the plant life of a region, and botany fixed it as a technical collective noun.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 vegetation，指一地的植物，植物学随后把它固定为技术性的集合名词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century physicians used vegetation for abnormal growths on valves and surfaces, borrowing the image of something sprouting.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，医生用 vegetation 指瓣膜与体表上的异常生长物，借的是「冒出来生长」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link of vegere to vigere 'to be vigorous' is generally believed but not demonstrated, and the first English date for the botanical sense is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：vegere 与 vigere「强健」的联系一般认为成立，却未经证实；植物义在英语中的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share the Latin root from one false friend; group two holds the words used for plant cover in ecology.
note.cn: 第一组区分共用拉丁词根的外形相近词与一个假朋友；第二组是生态学里指植物覆盖的近义词。

entries.definition: From vegetare, but in English it means to live a dull, inactive life or, of plants, simply to grow.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 vegetare，但在英语里指过呆板无所事事的生活，或指植物生长。

entries.definition: From Latin vegetabilis 'animating', the same root, but the noun settled on a garden crop.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vegetabilis「有生气的」，词根相同，名词却落在园圃作物上。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of plants' or 'plant-like', closer to the Latin source than vegetation is.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「植物的、像植物的」，比 vegetation 更贴近拉丁原义。

entries.definition: From venerari 'to worship', with no plant meaning at all; only the sound overlaps.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 venerari「敬拜」，与植物无关，只有读音重叠。

entries.definition: The plant species of a region listed by name; vegetation is the living cover itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区按名称列出的植物物种；vegetation 指活生生的覆盖本身。

entries.definition: Green plants seen as pleasant colour; it is a look, while vegetation is an ecological mass.
entries.definitionCN: 把绿色植物当作悦目的颜色；它说的是一种外观，vegetation 说的是生态整体。

entries.definition: A neutral everyday phrase with no technical edge; vegetation is its scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的日常说法，不带技术色彩；vegetation 是它的科学对应词。

entries.definition: The total mass of living material, measured by weight; vegetation names the cover, not the weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指活物质的总质量，按重量计；vegetation 指覆盖，不指重量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin family and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的拉丁词族与真实搭配，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: vegetare 'to enliven' + -ation: the state of ground made lively by plants.
normal.cn: vegetare「使有生气」+ -ation：土地被植物弄得有生气的状态。

normal.en: The family: vegetate, vegetative, vegetational, vegetated.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetate、vegetative、vegetational、vegetated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: natural vegetation, dense vegetation, sparse vegetation, native vegetation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：天然植被、茂密植被、稀疏植被、乡土植被。

normal.en: The same root gives vegetable and vegetal, both about plant life.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 vegetable 与 vegetal，都与植物有关。

normal.en: Medical charts speak of a vegetation on a valve, a sprout where nothing should sprout.
normal.cn: 病历上说瓣膜上有赘生物，即在不该长的地方长出一块。

abstract.en: Picture a lawn so thick that you cannot see the soil beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片厚到看不见下面泥土的草坪。

abstract.en: Picture a green blanket laid over a wound in the land.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿毯盖在土地的伤口上。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf where every plant of a valley is filed as one volume.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上有一卷书，把一个谷地的植物全归档在里面。

examples.en: Fires every few years keep the vegetation short and diverse.
examples.cn: 每隔几年烧一次，植被就保持低矮而多样。

examples.en: Loose vegetation was cleared before the foundations were poured.
examples.cn: 浇筑地基之前，松散的植被已被清除。

examples.en: The valley's vegetation shifts from grass to oak as you climb.
examples.cn: 沿山坡向上，谷地植被从草类变为橡树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维基（veget）+ 生长（ation）」——地上长满绿色档案 → 植被

root: 拉丁 vegetare「使有生气、促使生长」＝ vegere「有活力」＋反复后缀；vegetatio 指「生长」。vegere 更深来源不确定，与 vigere「强健」的联系一般认为成立但未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is made lively, the ground is covered, the cover is classified, mapped, cleared, and finally read either as disease or as climate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先使某处有生气，再铺满地面，然后被分类、绘图、清除，最后或被读成疾病，或被读成气候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a living quilt spread over the ground, growing from below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一床铺在地面上的活被子，从下面长上来。

branches.en: QUICKENING: the root sense is making a place lively, whether mildly or rankly.
branches.cn: 使有生气：词根义就是让某处活起来，无论温和还是过盛。

branches.en: COVER: roots bind the surface, so the mass becomes a protective layer.
branches.cn: 覆盖：根抓住地表，整体于是成为保护层。

branches.en: CLASSIFY: ecology names formations, then fixes them into surveys.
branches.cn: 分类：生态学先给群系命名，再把它们固定为调查资料。

branches.en: OBSTACLE: what blocks a project turns from ecosystem into material to be removed.
branches.cn: 障碍：挡住工程的部分，从生态系统变成待清材料。

branches.en: TWO READINGS: growth may be disease in a body or evidence of ancient climate in mud.
branches.cn: 两种读法：生长既可能是体内的病，也可能是泥里的古气候证据。

intro.en: Vegetation is built from a Latin verb stem plus a noun suffix, and that stem also builds several everyday English words.
intro.cn: vegetation 由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀构成，这个词干还构成若干日常英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegere 'to be lively' gives vegetus, vegetare, vegetatio; the suffix -ation marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegere「有生气」给出 vegetus、vegetare、vegetatio；后缀 -ation 表示动作或其结果。

items.example: The bare stem carries the idea of life.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的词干带着「活」的意思。

items.example: The adjective describes ground that is full of growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述长满植物的土地。

items.example: Warm rain vegetates the dry slope.
The noun names the process, not the plants.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指过程，不指植物。

items.meaning: action or result of an action
items.example: It turns a verb stem into a nameable state.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词词干变成可命名的状态。

items.meaning: the state of ground made lively
to grow, or to live dully
items.example: Moss vegetates on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 苔藓在背阴的墙上生长。

items.meaning: tending to grow rather than reproduce

items.example: The vegetated bank held the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满植物的河岸保住了土壤。

definition_zh: 营养生长的；无性繁殖的；植物状态的；自主神经的（旧称）
definition_en: relating to growth and nutrition rather than reproduction; in medicine, lacking conscious activity; in older anatomy, involuntary
core_image: 一株植物只顾长根长叶，不开花也不结果，全部力气都花在「把身体做大」上
scene: 这株植物不靠种子，而靠地下横走的茎不断冒出新的植株；园艺上把这种繁殖方式与开花结果相区分。The plant spreads by vegetative shoots rather than by seed.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetative 指「营养生长的、以根茎叶的伸长来繁殖的」（第 3 个义项：不经有性过程的营养繁殖）；句意为这株植物靠营养枝而非种子蔓延。

pos.zh: 营养生长的；无性繁殖的
（医学）植物状态的；无意识活动的
（旧称）自主神经的；不随意的

senses.title: Growing rather than reproducing
senses.titleCN: 只管长身体，不进入繁殖
senses.definition: concerned with growth and nutrition rather than with flowering or reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 与生长、营养有关，而非与开花繁殖有关
senses.example: Pruning shifts the tree from vegetative growth to fruit production.
senses.exampleCN: 修剪让这棵树从营养生长转向结果。
senses.why: Vegetative labels the part of a plant's life that builds the body; reproduction is the other part, and the two compete for the same energy.
senses.whyCN: vegetative 标出植物生命中「造身体」的那一半；繁殖是另一半，两者争夺同一份能量。

senses.title: A state without conscious activity
senses.titleCN: 只剩身体机能、没有意识的状态
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a person shows no conscious activity
senses.definitionCN: 人没有意识活动、只余身体机能的医学状态
senses.example: He remained in a vegetative state for months.
senses.exampleCN: 他在植物状态中躺了几个月。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the plant image: a body that breathes and digests but does not think is alive the way a plant is alive.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了植物的意象：会呼吸、会消化却不思考的身体，像植物那样活着。

senses.title: Reproduction by shoots, not seed
senses.titleCN: 用根茎叶直接长出新株的繁殖方式
senses.definition: reproduction by roots, stems or leaves rather than by seed
senses.definitionCN: 以根、茎、叶而非种子产生新个体的繁殖方式
senses.example: The plant spreads by vegetative shoots rather than by seed.
senses.exampleCN: 这株植物靠营养枝而非种子蔓延。
senses.why: Because a shoot carries the parent's full genetic make-up, botanists call this growth-as-reproduction, hence vegetative.
senses.whyCN: 因为一条枝带着母株的完整遗传信息，植物学家把这种「生长即繁殖」称为营养繁殖。

senses.title: The non-reproductive phase
senses.titleCN: 一生中尚未开花的阶段
senses.definition: the period of a plant's life before flowering begins
senses.definitionCN: 植物开花之前的那段生活史
senses.example: Long days shorten the vegetative phase in some cereals.
senses.exampleCN: 长日照缩短了某些谷物的营养生长期。
senses.why: Once a plant is timed by seasons, its life splits into a building phase and a breeding phase, and the first keeps the old name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦植物受季节支配，一生就分成「建造期」与「繁殖期」，前者沿用旧名。

senses.title: Propagation by cuttings
senses.titleCN: 用切下的枝叶根繁育新株
senses.definition: multiplication of plants from cuttings, division or grafting
senses.definitionCN: 用插条、分株或嫁接来增殖植株
senses.example: Gardeners use vegetative propagation for identical apples.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺师用营养繁殖得到一模一样的苹果。
senses.why: Horticulture needs copies, not offspring; a vegetative method copies the parent exactly, which is why the word is prized there.
senses.whyCN: 园艺要的是复制品而非后代；营养繁殖能精确复制母株，这正是这个词在园艺里受重视的原因。

senses.title: Dormant or resting plant tissue
senses.titleCN: 处于休眠、只维持生命的状态
senses.definition: of tissue, alive but resting and showing only basic maintenance
senses.definitionCN: 组织活着却休眠、只做基本维持
senses.example: A vegetative bud waits under the bark until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 一个营养芽在树皮下等到春天。
senses.why: When growth pauses without dying, the word describes the low setting of life rather than its absence.
senses.whyCN: 当生长停住却没死，这个词描述的是生命的低档运转，而不是生命的缺席。

senses.title: Of involuntary nerve function
senses.titleCN: 指不随意的神经活动（旧术语）
senses.definition: relating to the involuntary nervous system, an older medical usage
senses.definitionCN: 与不随意神经系统有关，属旧式医学用法
senses.example: Older texts call it the vegetative nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献称其为自主神经系统。
senses.why: The older label treats digestion and circulation as the body's plant-like housekeeping, running without a decision.
senses.whyCN: 这个旧称把消化与循环看成身体「像植物一样的家务」，无需谁来做决定。

senses.title: Bare, monotonous, merely existing
senses.titleCN: 形容生活只剩吃喝睡、毫无波澜
senses.definition: describing a life or place that only maintains itself, with no interest or event
senses.definitionCN: 形容生活或地方只维持自身，没有兴致也没有事件
senses.example: The town felt vegetative, all routine and no occasion.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇显得沉闷，全是例行公事，没有一件值得说的事。
senses.why: The figurative use borrows the plant state: functions continue, but nothing is initiated, and the tone is mildly disparaging.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法借的是植物状态：机能继续，却没有任何主动的开端，语气略带贬义。

intro.en: Vegetative comes from Medieval Latin vegetativus 'giving life, growing', from vegetare 'to enliven'. The medical and botanical uses split in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: vegetative 来自中世纪拉丁 vegetativus「赋予生命、促使生长」，源于 vegetare「使有生气」。医学与植物学的用法在 19 世纪分开。

items.en: Vegetare 'to enliven, animate' is the base verb, itself from vegetus 'lively'.
items.cn: vegetare「使有生气、使活动」是基础动词，再往前是 vegetus「有活力的」。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed vegetativus for the power that makes a body grow and stay alive.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构出 vegetativus，指使身体生长并维持生命的力。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fourteenth century in the sense of 'giving life', applied to nourishment and warmth.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个形容词，义为「赋予生命的」，用于营养与温热。

items.en: From the eighteenth century botanists used it for growth opposed to reproduction, and the phrase vegetative reproduction followed.
items.cn: 18 世纪起，植物学家用它指与繁殖相对的生长，「营养繁殖」一语随后出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine applied it to patients who breathe but do not respond, and to the nerves that work without conscious control.
items.cn: 19 世纪医学把它用于会呼吸却无反应的病人，也用于不随意控制的神经。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and root): the exact first English citation for each specialised sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of vegere remains unsettled, so any root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：各专门义的确切首见书证并无定论；vegere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦未确定，凡给出的词根形式都是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns that look alike but diverge in sense or root; group two holds words for unconscious or inactive states.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近而词义或词根有别的形容词与名词；第二组指无意识或不活动的状态。

entries.definition: The mass noun for plant cover; the adjective describes the growing, non-reproductive side of plants.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物覆盖的集合名词；形容词则描述植物生长而非繁殖的一面。

entries.definition: Means 'of plants' in general, with no technical split between growth and reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指「植物的」，不含生长与繁殖的技术区分。

entries.definition: A person who eats no meat, built on vegetable from the same Latin stem but far from botany.
entries.definitionCN: 指不吃肉的人，由同出该拉丁词干的 vegetable 构成，与植物学已相距很远。

entries.definition: From vita 'life'; it means necessary for life, not plant-like growth.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 vita「生命」，意为维持生命所必需，不指植物式生长。

entries.definition: The general word for lacking awareness; vegetative is the narrower clinical stage.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指失去意识；vegetative 是更窄的临床分度。

entries.definition: Means unable to act or move, often of matter; it lacks the 'still alive' part.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能活动，多用于物质，缺了「仍然活着」这一层。

entries.definition: A resting state that will resume; vegetative tissue may also be dormant, but vegetative stresses maintenance.
entries.definitionCN: 指会恢复的休眠；营养组织也可能休眠，但 vegetative 强调维持。

entries.definition: A literal description with no Latin flavour; vegetative is the technical term for the same contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 字面描述，不带拉丁色彩；vegetative 是表达同一对照的术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations are the real Latin family and the real collocations of botany and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想是真实的拉丁词族，以及植物学与医学中的真实搭配。

normal.en: vegetare 'to enliven' + -ive: having the power to make grow.
normal.cn: vegetare「使有生气」+ -ive：具有使之生长的力。

normal.en: The family: vegetation, vegetate, vegetatively, vegetated.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetation、vegetate、vegetatively、vegetated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: vegetative growth, vegetative reproduction, vegetative state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：营养生长、营养繁殖、植物状态。

normal.en: Botany pairs it with reproductive: one builds the body, the other makes the seed.
normal.cn: 植物学把它与 reproductive 对举：一个造身体，一个结种子。

normal.en: Medicine reuses the plant image for a body that breathes but does not respond.
normal.cn: 医学把这套植物意象再用到会呼吸却无反应的身体上。

abstract.en: Picture a body lying still while its heartbeat keeps its own routine.
abstract.cn: 想象一具静止的身体，心跳照自己的常规走着。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that keeps widening but never bears fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵不断长粗却从不结果的树。

abstract.en: Picture a machine set to idle, running but producing nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一台调到怠速的机器，转着却不出活。

examples.en: Cut back the vegetative growth so the plant can flower.
examples.cn: 剪掉营养生长，让植物得以开花。

examples.en: The patient moved from a coma into a vegetative state.
examples.cn: 病人从昏迷进入植物状态。

examples.en: Strawberries propagate vegetatively by runners.
examples.cn: 草莓靠匍匐茎进行营养繁殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蔬菜（veget）+ 活着（ative）」——只会长身子、不开花 → 营养生长的；植物状态的

root: 中世纪拉丁 vegetativus「赋予生命、促使生长」，来自 vegetare「使有生气」；再往前为 vegetus「有活力的」，vegere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from one contrast: growth and maintenance on one side, reproduction and conscious action on the other, until the word finally means merely existing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都来自同一个对照：一边是生长与维持，另一边是繁殖与有意识行动；最后这个词引申为「只是存在着」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant spending everything on roots and leaves, never on flower or seed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株植物把所有力气花在根和叶上，从不用在花与种子上。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: the adjective marks the growing half, then the half that stays alive without awareness.
branches.cn: 两面：形容词先标出「生长」的一半，再标出「活着却无意识」的一半。

branches.en: NO SEED: growth itself becomes a way of multiplying, and a phase before flowering.
branches.cn: 不结种：生长本身成了增殖方式，也成了开花前的阶段。

branches.en: GARDEN USE: cuttings copy a parent, while dormant tissue only waits.
branches.cn: 园艺用法：插条复制母株，休眠组织只是等待。

branches.en: OLD ANATOMY: housekeeping nerves run like plant functions, without decision.
branches.cn: 旧解剖学：家务式的神经像植物机能那样运转，无需决定。

branches.en: FIGURE: a life that maintains itself and initiates nothing.
branches.cn: 比喻：只维持自身、不发起任何事的生活。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin participle stem plus -ive; the same stem builds the whole vegetation family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁分词词干加 -ive；同一词干构成整个 vegetation 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegetare 'to enliven' yields vegetativus; -ivus marks a tendency or capacity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegetare「使有生气」给出 vegetativus；-ivus 表示倾向或能力。

items.example: The stem is about life, not about plants alone.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干说的是生命，不只说植物。

items.meaning: tending to, having the power to
items.example: It names a capacity rather than an act.
items.exampleCN: 它命名的是能力，不是动作。

items.example: The word entered English from this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语正是从这个形式借入。
这株植物以营养方式蔓延。

items.example: A vegetated strip filtered the runoff.
items.exampleCN: 一条长满植物的带子过滤了径流。

definition_zh: 植被覆盖；植被覆盖层；植被覆盖度
definition_en: the layer of plants covering the ground, or the share of ground that such plants cover
core_image: 从空中俯看，地面被一块块绿色补丁盖住，裸露的土只在缝隙里露出
scene: 从高空俯看，绿色补丁连成片的地方土不易被冲走，补丁破碎的地方沟壑开始出现；研究者用这种差别判断土地退化的程度。Satellite images show vegetation cover shrinking along the river.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetation cover 指「地表被植物覆盖的整体状况」（第 1 个义项：作为一层覆盖物看待的植被）；句意为卫星影像显示沿河一带的植被覆盖正在缩减。

pos.zh: 植被覆盖（层）；植被覆盖度

senses.title: The plant layer over the ground
senses.titleCN: 贴地铺开的植物层
senses.definition: the layer of plants that lies over the soil surface
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在土壤表面的植物层
senses.example: Thick vegetation cover kept the slope from sliding.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的植被覆盖使山坡没有滑动。
senses.why: The phrase joins a mass noun for plants to a noun for a lid: what plants do to soil is throw a lid over it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把指植物的集合名词与指盖子的名词连在一起：植物对土壤做的事，就是给它盖上一层。

senses.title: The percentage of ground covered
senses.titleCN: 被植物盖住的地面所占的成数
senses.definition: the proportion of an area covered by plants, usually given as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 一个区域内被植物覆盖的比例，通常按百分数给出
senses.example: Vegetation cover fell from sixty to thirty percent in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间植被覆盖度从六成降到三成。
senses.why: Once the layer is measured, the phrase shifts from the lid to a number: how much of the ground wears it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这层被测量，短语就从「盖子」转为「数值」：地面有多大比例盖着它。

senses.title: A mapped layer in remote sensing
senses.titleCN: 遥感图上单独画出的一层
senses.definition: the plant layer as a separate class in a satellite or GIS map
senses.definitionCN: 卫星或地理信息图中单独分出的植物图层
senses.example: The map overlays vegetation cover on the rainfall grid.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅地图把植被覆盖叠在降水网格上。
senses.why: Digital mapping turns the living lid into a coloured layer that can be switched on and off beside other layers.
senses.whyCN: 数字制图把这层活盖子变成可与其他图层一起开关的彩色图层。

senses.title: A shield for topsoil
senses.titleCN: 挡雨挡风、护住表土的那层
senses.definition: the layer understood by what it protects, namely the soil beneath it
senses.definitionCN: 从所保护的表土来理解的那一层植物
senses.example: Vegetation cover keeps the topsoil from washing away.
senses.exampleCN: 植被覆盖使表土不被冲走。
senses.why: In soil science the phrase names a service rather than an object: the roots and litter hold grains in place.
senses.whyCN: 在土壤学里，这个短语命名的是一种功能而非物件：根与落叶层把土粒固定住。

senses.title: A cover type or structure
senses.titleCN: 按形态划分的覆盖类别
senses.definition: a class of cover defined by growth form, such as woody or grass cover
senses.definitionCN: 按生长形态划分的覆盖类别，如木本或草本覆盖
senses.example: Woody vegetation cover reacts differently from grass cover.
senses.exampleCN: 木本植被覆盖与草本覆盖的反应不同。
senses.why: Classifying the lid by its builders lets ecologists compare places that look alike from above but differ in species.
senses.whyCN: 按「建造者」给盖子分类，生态学家就能比较从空中看相似、物种却不同的地方。

senses.title: Cover tracked through time
senses.titleCN: 被连续观测以看变化的那层
senses.definition: the layer followed over years to detect gain or loss
senses.definitionCN: 连年跟踪以判断增加或减少的那层植物
senses.example: Repeat flights track vegetation cover after grazing stops.
senses.exampleCN: 停止放牧后，重复航拍跟踪植被覆盖。
senses.why: Monitoring treats the lid as a signal: if it closes over bare ground, the land is recovering.
senses.whyCN: 监测把这层盖子当作信号：它若在裸地上合拢，说明土地正在恢复。

senses.title: Cover restored by protection
senses.titleCN: 经封育、补植而重新长回的那层
senses.definition: the layer rebuilt by fencing, reseeding or grazing control
senses.definitionCN: 通过围封、补播或控制放牧重新长出的植物层
senses.example: Fencing let vegetation cover return within five years.
senses.exampleCN: 围封之后，植被覆盖在五年内恢复。
senses.why: Restoration speaks of the phrase as a goal, something a manager can bring back rather than merely measure.
senses.whyCN: 恢复语境把它当作目标，是管理者能重新带回来的东西，而不只是测量对象。

senses.title: Cover lost through overuse
senses.titleCN: 因过度放牧或开垦而消失的那层
senses.definition: the layer removed by overgrazing, clearing or drought
senses.definitionCN: 因过度放牧、开垦或干旱而丧失的植物层
senses.example: Overgrazing strips vegetation cover from the upper slope.
senses.exampleCN: 过度放牧剥去了上坡的植被覆盖。
senses.why: Loss reverses the lid image: the ground is uncovered again, and every agent of erosion gets direct access.
senses.whyCN: 丧失把盖子的意象倒过来：地面重新裸露，各种侵蚀力量直接触及它。

intro.en: The phrase is modern, but both parts are old: vegetation from Latin vegetare 'to enliven', cover from Latin cooperire 'to cover completely'.
intro.cn: 这个短语是现代组合，两部分都很古老：vegetation 来自拉丁 vegetare「使有生气」，cover 来自拉丁 cooperire「完全盖住」。

items.en: Vegetatio 'growth, a making lively' supplied vegetation, the plant mass of a place.
items.cn: vegetatio「生长、使有生气」提供了 vegetation，即一地的植物整体。

items.en: Cooperire 'to cover wholly' is co- 'together, completely' plus operire 'to close, cover'.
items.cn: cooperire「完全盖住」由 co-「完全」与 operire「关上、遮住」构成。

items.en: Old French covrir gave English cover in the thirteenth century, first as a verb, later as a noun.
items.cn: 古法语 covrir 在 13 世纪给出英语 cover，先作动词，后作名词。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology and remote sensing joined the two words to name the plant layer over soil and its measured share.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学与遥感把这两个词连起来，命名土壤之上的植物层及其测得比例。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and root): the exact first use of the compound is not fixed, and the deeper origin of Latin operire is disputed, so any older root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：这个复合形式的确切首用年代没有定论；拉丁 operire 的更深来源有争议，凡为其给出的更古老词根都是重构形式。

note.en: Group one contrasts look-alikes built on cover or on the same Latin stem; group two holds the neighbouring terms of land description.
note.cn: 第一组对比由 cover 或同一拉丁词干构成的外形相近词；第二组是土地描述中的邻近术语。

entries.definition: From cover plus -age: the extent something reaches, as insurance coverage; it measures reach, not plants.
entries.definitionCN: 由 cover 加 -age 构成：指某事物达到的范围，如保险覆盖；它量的是范围，不是植物。

entries.tag: same root, plain verb or noun
entries.definition: The simple word for putting something over something else; it says nothing about plants.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物盖在另一物上的简单词，不含植物的意思。

entries.definition: From Latin cooperire too, but it means concealed or a hiding place, not a plant layer.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自拉丁 cooperire，却指隐蔽的或藏身处，不是植物层。

entries.definition: Old French covrir plus lit 'bed': a bedspread, a lid for a bed rather than for soil.
entries.definitionCN: 古法语 covrir 加 lit「床」：床罩，盖的是床不是土。

entries.definition: The full classification of what lies on the ground, including water, rock and buildings; vegetation cover is one class within it.
entries.definitionCN: 对地表一切覆盖物的完整分类，含水、岩石与建筑；植被覆盖只是其中一类。

entries.definition: The share of ground shaded by tree crowns, measured from above; it ignores low plants.
entries.definitionCN: 树冠遮住地面的比例，从上方测量，不计低矮植物。

entries.definition: Low-growing plants that hide bare soil; it names the plants, while vegetation cover also names the measured share.
entries.definitionCN: 遮住裸土的低矮植物；它指植物本身，植被覆盖还指测得的比例。

entries.definition: The plants of an area as a whole; adding cover turns the mass into a layer with a measurable extent.
entries.definitionCN: 一地植物的整体；加上 cover 后，整体变成有可测范围的一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations are the real parts of the compound and the real terms of ecology.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用这个复合词的真实构成部分与生态学真实术语。

normal.en: vegetation 'plant mass' + cover 'lid': a lid of plants over soil.
normal.cn: vegetation「植物整体」+ cover「盖子」：盖在土上的一层植物。

normal.en: The family: vegetation, cover, coverage, cover crop.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetation、cover、coverage、cover crop。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: vegetation cover change, vegetation cover loss, vegetation cover map.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：植被覆盖变化、植被覆盖丧失、植被覆盖图。

normal.en: Latin cooperire 'to cover wholly' is co- plus operire, so cover already means a complete lid.
normal.cn: 拉丁 cooperire「完全盖住」是 co- 加 operire，可见 cover 本身就含「完全盖上」。

normal.en: Remote sensing treats it as one switchable layer beside rainfall and slope.
normal.cn: 遥感把它当作降水、坡度旁边一个可开关的图层。

abstract.en: Picture a green patchwork quilt whose holes show bare brown soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一床绿色拼布被，破洞里露出褐色的裸土。

abstract.en: Picture a percentage written on that quilt, saying how much of the bed it covers.
abstract.cn: 想象那床被子上写着一个百分数，说明它盖住了床的多少。

abstract.en: Picture a scab forming over a cut in the land until the surface closes.
abstract.cn: 想象土地的一道伤口上结出痂，直到表面合拢。

examples.en: Grazing pressure reduced vegetation cover across the plateau.
examples.cn: 放牧压力使高原各处的植被覆盖减少。

examples.en: The report maps vegetation cover against soil loss.
examples.cn: 报告把植被覆盖与土壤流失对照制图。

examples.en: Willows raised vegetation cover on the sandbank within three seasons.
examples.cn: 柳树在三个季节内提高了沙洲的植被覆盖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「植被 + 盖子」——给土地盖上一层绿被子，还量出盖了多少 → 植被覆盖

root: vegetation 来自拉丁 vegetatio「生长」，cover 来自拉丁 cooperire「完全盖住」（co- + operire）；operire 更深来源有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the lid itself to the percentage it covers, then to its map, its service, its types, its gain, and finally its loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「盖子」本身，转到它覆盖的百分比，再到它的图、它的功能、它的类型、它的增加，最后到它的丧失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green lid laid over bare ground, seen from above as a patchwork.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层盖在裸地上的绿色盖子，从空中看像拼布。

branches.en: LID AND NUMBER: the same phrase names the layer and then the share of ground it hides.
branches.cn: 盖子与数字：同一短语既指那层，也指它遮住的地面比例。

branches.en: MAP AND TYPE: remote sensing makes it a layer, ecology splits that layer into growth forms.
branches.cn: 图层与类型：遥感把它做成图层，生态学再把图层按生长型拆分。

branches.en: SERVICE: the layer is read by what it protects, the topsoil below.
branches.cn: 功能：这层按它所保护的下方表土来理解。

branches.en: GAIN: repeated flights and fencing both ask whether the lid is closing again.
branches.cn: 增加：重复航拍与围封都在问，这层盖子是否重新合拢。

branches.en: LOSS: removing the lid exposes the ground to wind and water.
branches.cn: 丧失：揭开盖子，地面就直接暴露给风与水。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: a Latin noun for plant growth plus a Latin verb for covering, each still productive in English.
intro.cn: 这个复合词是透明的：一个指植物生长的拉丁名词，加一个指覆盖的拉丁动词，两部分在英语中仍能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegetatio gives vegetation; Latin cooperire, through Old French covrir, gives cover and coverage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegetatio 给出 vegetation；拉丁 cooperire 经古法语 covrir 给出 cover 与 coverage。

items.example: The prefix makes the covering total.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使覆盖成为完全覆盖。

items.example: The Latin verb is the core of cover.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是 cover 的核心。
保险覆盖范围各不相同。

items.meaning: a crop grown to shield soil
items.example: Rye serves as a cover crop.

items.meaning: the measured share of plant cover

items.example: The coverer of the pit used boards.

definition_zh: 植物群；植物志；（人体）菌群
definition_en: the plant species of a region taken together; a book that lists them; the microbes living in or on a body
core_image: 一本按名字排列的名册，每个名字背后都站着一种真实生长的植物
scene: 岛上有些蕨类只在此处生长，别处找不到；植物志把它们逐一记下，供后来者比对。The island's flora includes ferns found nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 flora 指「一个地区植物物种的总和」（第 1 个义项：把一地植物种类整体看待）；句意为这座岛的植物群中有别处找不到的蕨类。

pos.zh: 植物群；植物区系
植物志（书名）
（人体）菌群

senses.title: All plant species of a region
senses.titleCN: 一个地区植物种类的总和
senses.definition: the whole set of plant species growing in a region
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物物种
senses.example: The island's flora includes ferns found nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的植物群中有别处找不到的蕨类。
senses.why: Flora began as the name of a goddess; naturalists then used it for the whole roll-call of plants in one place.
senses.whyCN: flora 原是女神之名；博物学家随后用它指一个地方全部植物的名录。

senses.title: A book listing those plants
senses.titleCN: 列出这些植物的书
senses.definition: a book or catalogue describing the plants of an area
senses.definitionCN: 描述某地植物的书或名录
senses.example: The county flora runs to eight hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 该郡的植物志长达八百页。
senses.why: The title of a catalogue was read as the name of its subject, so the same word names both the plants and the volume about them.
senses.whyCN: 书名被读成所写对象的名字，于是同一个词既指植物，也指写它们的书。

senses.title: Microbes of the gut
senses.titleCN: 肠道里的微生物群
senses.definition: the community of bacteria living in the intestines
senses.definitionCN: 生活在肠道里的细菌群落
senses.example: Antibiotics can disturb the gut flora for months.
senses.exampleCN: 抗生素可能扰动肠道菌群数月。
senses.why: Medicine extended the plant-roll-call image to invisible residents: a body, too, has a local list of species.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这套「地方物种名录」的意象扩展到看不见的居民：身体也有一份本地物种清单。

senses.title: Microbes of skin or mouth
senses.titleCN: 皮肤或口腔的微生物群
senses.definition: the resident microbes of a body surface or cavity
senses.definitionCN: 体表或腔内的常驻微生物
senses.example: The skin flora shifts with soap and humidity.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤菌群随肥皂与湿度而变。
senses.why: Each body surface keeps its own roster, so clinicians speak of a flora rather than a single germ.
senses.whyCN: 每个体表都保有自己的名册，因此临床说的是「菌群」而非单一细菌。

senses.title: The study of regional plant lists
senses.titleCN: 研究地区植物名录的学问
senses.definition: the branch of botany that compares the species lists of regions
senses.definitionCN: 比较各地区物种名录的植物学分支
senses.example: Floristics maps where each species first appears.
senses.exampleCN: 植物区系学标出每个物种首次出现的地方。
senses.why: Once lists exist, they can be compared, and comparison becomes a discipline with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 名录一旦存在就可以比较，而比较本身成为一门有名字的学问。

senses.title: Plants of a past period
senses.titleCN: 某一地质时期的植物群
senses.definition: the plant species reconstructed for a past geological period
senses.definitionCN: 重建出的某一地质时期的植物物种
senses.example: The fossil flora is dominated by seed ferns.
senses.exampleCN: 这一化石植物群以种子蕨为主。
senses.why: Fossils are read as a former roll-call, so a vanished world gets a flora of its own.
senses.whyCN: 化石被读作一份过去的点名册，消失的世界于是也有了自己的植物群。

senses.title: The Roman goddess of flowers
senses.titleCN: 罗马的花神
senses.definition: the Roman goddess of flowers and spring
senses.definitionCN: 罗马神话中司花与春天的女神
senses.example: The festival honoured Flora with garlands.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆用花环致敬花神。
senses.why: The common noun comes straight from the goddess, whose name already meant flower.
senses.whyCN: 这个普通名词直接来自女神之名，而女神之名本义就是花。

senses.title: Plants and animals named together
senses.titleCN: 与动物并称时的植物一侧
senses.definition: plants as one half of the pair flora and fauna
senses.definitionCN: 作为「动植物」一对中的植物一侧
senses.example: The reserve protects its flora and fauna alike.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区对动植物一并加以保护。
senses.why: Pairing the two Roman names gives a compact formula for all living things in a place.
senses.whyCN: 把两个罗马名字配对，就得到一个指一地全部生物的紧凑说法。

intro.en: Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers; her name comes from Latin flos, florem 'flower'. The botanical sense is early modern.
intro.cn: flora 是罗马的花神；其名来自拉丁 flos、florem「花」。植物学义属近代早期。

items.en: Flos, florem meant 'flower, blossom'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the forms sometimes proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: flos、florem 意为「花、开花」。其更深来源没有定论，有时为它提出的形式都是重构形式。

items.en: Flora was the goddess of flowers and of spring; her festival was the Floralia.
items.cn: Flora 是司花与春天的女神，她的节庆是花神节。

items.en: Early modern botanists titled their catalogues after her, and the book title slid into the sense 'plants of a region'.
items.cn: 近代早期植物学家用她的名字给名录命名，书名又滑入「一地的植物」之义。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century medicine applied the word to the resident microbes of gut, skin and mouth.
items.cn: 19 世纪后期起，医学把这个词用于肠道、皮肤与口腔的常驻微生物。

items.en: Flora and fauna became a fixed pair in English for the living things of a place.
items.cn: flora and fauna 在英语中成为指一地生物的固定搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of flos is unsettled, and the first English use of flora for regional plants is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：flos 在拉丁语之前的来源未定；flora 指地区植物在英语中的首用年代只有约数。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share the flower root from one that does not; group two holds the ecological neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组区分共用「花」词根的外形相近词与一个不同源词；第二组是生态学上的邻近词。

entries.definition: From flos: relating to flowers, as a floral scent; it describes flowers, not a species list.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 flos：与花有关的，如花香；它描述花，不指物种名录。

entries.definition: From floridus 'flowing with flowers': once 'flowering', now 'ornate' or 'ruddy'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 floridus「开满花的」：曾指「开花的」，今指「华丽」或「脸色红润」。

entries.definition: Originally the flower, the finest part of ground grain; the spelling split off with the food sense.
entries.definitionCN: 原指「花」，即磨碎谷物最精细的部分；拼写随食物义分化。

entries.definition: From Old English flor 'ground, pavement', unrelated to flos; only the sound matches.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 flor「地面、铺地」，与 flos 无关，只有读音相同。

entries.definition: The living plant cover of a place; flora is the species roll-call behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一地活生生的植物覆盖；flora 是它背后的物种名录。

entries.definition: The animal species of a region, paired with flora but never a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指一地的动物物种，与 flora 配对，却从不同义。

entries.definition: An everyday neutral phrase; flora is its technical and bookish counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 日常中性说法；flora 是它的技术、书面对应词。

entries.definition: The variety of living things measured as a count; flora is one roster within that total.
entries.definitionCN: 按数量衡量的生物多样性；flora 是这一总数中的一份名录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations are the real Latin root, the real goddess and the real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁词根、真实神名与真实搭配。

normal.en: Latin flos 'flower' gives Flora, floral, florist, floriculture and flora itself.
normal.cn: 拉丁 flos「花」给出 Flora、floral、florist、floriculture 与 flora。

normal.en: The family: floral, florist, floriculture, floristics.
normal.cn: 同族：floral、florist、floriculture、floristics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: native flora, local flora, gut flora, flora and fauna.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：本土植物群、地方植物群、肠道菌群、动植物。

normal.en: The goddess Flora lent her name to catalogues, and the catalogue lent it to the plants.
normal.cn: 花神 Flora 把名字借给名录，名录又把名字借给植物。

normal.en: Medicine reuses it for microbes, giving gut flora and skin flora.
normal.cn: 医学把它再用到微生物，于是有肠道菌群与皮肤菌群。

abstract.en: Picture a region's plants standing in a queue, each waiting to be named.
abstract.cn: 想象一个地区的植物排成队，等着被点名。

abstract.en: Picture the word as a passport listing every species allowed to live in one country.
abstract.cn: 想象这个词是一本护照，列出允许居留于一国的每个物种。

abstract.en: Picture a body as a garden with its own invisible planting list.
abstract.cn: 想象身体是一座花园，有自己的隐形种植清单。

examples.en: The flora of the wetlands includes three protected orchids.
examples.cn: 湿地植物群中有三种受保护的兰花。

examples.en: She wrote the flora of the whole archipelago.
examples.cn: 她写下了整个群岛的植物志。

examples.en: A high-fibre diet feeds a healthier gut flora.
examples.cn: 高纤维饮食养出更健康的肠道菌群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗洛拉（Flora）花神」——花神手里的花名册 → 植物群；植物志

root: 拉丁 flos、florem「花」，罗马花神 Flora 即由此得名；flos 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the goddess and her flower name, pass through the species list and the book that holds it, then extend to microbes and to a paired formula for all life.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从花神与「花」这个词开始，经过物种名录与承载名录的书，再扩展到微生物，最后成为指全部生物的配对说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a roll-call of flowers, written down and then applied to any living roster.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份花的点名册，先被写下来，再被用于任何活物的名册。

branches.en: LIST AND BOOK: the plants and the volume about them share one name.
branches.cn: 名录与书：植物本身与写它们的书共用一个名字。

branches.en: INVISIBLE RESIDENTS: the roster moves from forests to the body's microbes.
branches.cn: 看不见的居民：名册从森林移到体内的微生物。

branches.en: COMPARE ACROSS TIME: species lists of regions and of past periods can both be compared.
branches.cn: 跨时间比较：地区名录与过去时期的名录都能拿来比较。

branches.en: GODDESS: the proper name is the source of the common noun.
branches.cn: 神名：专名是普通名词的来源。

branches.en: PAIR: flora beside fauna names all life in a place.
branches.cn: 配对：flora 与 fauna 并称，指一地全部生物。

intro.en: Flora and its family descend from one Latin noun for flower, with suffixes marking adjective, person and craft.
intro.cn: flora 及其词族都出自一个指「花」的拉丁名词，后缀标出形容词、人物与技艺。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos, florem 'flower' yields Flora, floralis, floricultura; -alis, -ista and -cultura build the derivatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flos、florem「花」给出 Flora、floralis、floricultura；-alis、-ista 与 -cultura 构成派生词。

items.example: The root names the part that makes seed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指结种的那一部分。
它把 floralis 变成 floral。

items.example: A floral scent filled the room.
It gives florist, a flower seller.

items.exampleCN: 花艺师给花茎缠了铁丝。
花卉栽培是一门大生意。
植物区系学比较物种名录。

definition_zh: 叶子（总称）；叶丛；装饰用枝叶
definition_en: the leaves of a plant or of many plants taken as a mass; cut branches used for decoration
core_image: 一棵树的所有叶片连成一片会摇动的绿色表面，风过时整片一起翻动
scene: 入秋以后叶片由绿转铜再转金，远看整片林子像被重新上了色。Autumn turns the foliage copper and gold.
sceneCN: 这里 foliage 指「一棵或一片植物上全部叶子的总称」（第 1 个义项：把叶子作为整体看待的叶丛）；句意为秋天把叶丛染成铜色与金色。

pos.zh: 叶子（总称）；叶丛
（花艺、装饰用）切叶

senses.title: All the leaves of a plant
senses.titleCN: 一株或一片植物的叶子的总称
senses.definition: the leaves of a plant or group of plants considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一株或一群植物的叶子作为整体看待
senses.example: Autumn turns the foliage copper and gold.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天把叶丛染成铜色与金色。
senses.why: Foliage is a collective noun: it never counts leaves one by one, it sees them as one surface.
senses.whyCN: foliage 是集合名词：它从不一片一片地数叶子，而是把叶子看成一张表面。

senses.title: The leafy canopy as a layer
senses.titleCN: 树冠里由叶子组成的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of leaves that fills a crown and shades what is below
senses.definitionCN: 树冠中填满枝叶、遮住下方的那一层
senses.example: Sparrows hid in the dense foliage of the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 麻雀藏在树篱茂密的叶丛里。
senses.why: Once the mass is seen from below or above, it becomes a layer with depth and shade, not just a list of parts.
senses.whyCN: 从下方或上方看这团叶子时，它就成了有厚度、有阴影的一层，而不只是一堆部件。

senses.title: Leaves valued for their colour
senses.titleCN: 因颜色而被观赏的叶子
senses.definition: leaves regarded as colour, especially in autumn or in ornamental planting
senses.definitionCN: 被当作色彩来欣赏的叶子，尤指秋叶或观赏栽植
senses.example: Tourists come for the autumn foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 游客为秋叶而来。
senses.why: When colour is the point, the word moves from botany to scenery, and the leaf becomes a patch of paint.
senses.whyCN: 当重点是颜色，这个词就从植物学移向风景，叶子也成了一块颜料。

senses.title: Cut branches for decoration
senses.titleCN: 剪下来作装饰的枝叶
senses.definition: stems and leaves cut for floristry or display
senses.definitionCN: 为花艺或陈列剪下的枝与叶
senses.example: The florist ordered cut foliage for the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 花艺师为大堂订了切叶。
senses.why: A trade term treats the mass as material: it is harvested, graded and sold like any other stock.
senses.whyCN: 行业术语把这团叶当材料：像别的货品一样采收、分级、出售。

senses.title: Leafy material eaten by animals
senses.titleCN: 被动物取食的枝叶
senses.definition: branches and leaves used as fodder
senses.definitionCN: 用作饲料的枝叶
senses.example: Goats browse the lower foliage of the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 山羊啃食树下部枝叶。
senses.why: Husbandry turns the same mass into feed, measured by what a animal can reach.
senses.whyCN: 畜牧把它变成饲料，按动物能够到的高度来衡量。

senses.title: Leaf ornament in art
senses.titleCN: 艺术中的叶形装饰
senses.definition: leaf forms used as ornament in architecture or design
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与设计中被用作装饰的叶形
senses.example: The capital is carved with acanthus foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 柱头刻着茛苕叶饰。
senses.why: Ornament keeps only the outline of leaves, so the word comes to mean a pattern rather than a plant.
senses.whyCN: 装饰只保留叶子的轮廓，词义于是变成图案而非植物。

senses.title: A plant grown for its leaves
senses.titleCN: 以观叶为目的栽种的植物
senses.definition: a plant cultivated mainly for its leaves rather than flowers
senses.definitionCN: 主要因叶而非花而栽种的植物
senses.example: Foliage plants fill the shaded border.
senses.exampleCN: 观叶植物填满了背阴花坛。
senses.why: Horticulture splits plants by the organ that sells, and the leaf group takes the mass noun as a label.
senses.whyCN: 园艺按出售的器官给植物分类，观叶这一类就用这个集合名词作标签。

senses.title: Cover and concealment
senses.titleCN: 被枝叶遮住而形成的掩蔽
senses.definition: the concealment that a mass of leaves provides
senses.definitionCN: 成片叶子提供的遮蔽
senses.example: The nest was lost in foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 巢藏在叶丛深处看不见。
senses.why: A mass thick enough to hide a nest becomes a place, so the word shifts from material to cover.
senses.whyCN: 厚到能藏住鸟巢的一团叶就成了一个地方，词义从材料转为掩蔽。

intro.en: Foliage comes from Old French feuillage, from feuille 'leaf', from Latin folium 'leaf'. The Latin noun is linked to Greek phyllon, but the deeper origin is unsettled.
intro.cn: foliage 来自古法语 feuillage，源于 feuille「叶」，再往前是拉丁 folium「叶」。这个拉丁名词与希腊 phyllon 有联系，但更深来源未定。

items.en: Folium meant 'leaf'. Its relation to Greek phyllon 'leaf' is generally believed, yet no single older root has been demonstrated.
items.cn: folium 意为「叶」。它与希腊 phyllon「叶」的联系一般认为成立，但更古老的单一词根尚未得到证明。

items.en: The plural folia 'leaves' was felt as a collective, which prepared the way for a mass noun.
items.cn: 复数 folia「叶子」有集合意味，为后来的集合名词铺了路。

items.en: Old French feuille 'leaf' kept the Latin sense; its collective derivative feuillage named the mass of leaves.
items.cn: 古法语 feuille「叶」保留了拉丁义；它的集合派生词 feuillage 指成片的叶。

items.en: English borrowed foliage in the sixteenth century for leaves in general, and later for cut branches in floristry.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 foliage，泛指叶子，后来又指花艺中的切叶。

items.en: Architectural handbooks extended it to carved leaf patterns, where only the outline survives.
items.cn: 建筑手册把它扩展到雕刻的叶形图案，那里只剩轮廓。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link between folium and phyllon is a general belief rather than a proven derivation, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：folium 与 phyllon 的联系只是一般看法，并非已证实的派生；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one separates relatives built on Latin folium from one false friend; group two holds words for leaves and leaf masses.
note.cn: 第一组区分由拉丁 folium 构成的同族词与一个假朋友；第二组指叶子与叶丛的说法。

entries.definition: From folium: a leaf of paper or a book format; the plant sense was lost when it named pages.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 folium：指一张纸或书的开本；转指纸页后植物义消失。

entries.definition: Portare 'to carry' plus folium: a case for loose sheets, now also a set of investments.
entries.definitionCN: portare「携带」加 folium：装散页的夹子，今也指一组投资。

entries.definition: Relating to leaves, as foliar feeding; it describes leaves rather than naming a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 与叶有关的，如叶面施肥；它描述叶，不命名叶丛。

entries.definition: From Latin filum 'thread', which gave the idea of a line of documents; nothing to do with leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 filum「线」，引申为一列文件，与叶子无关。

entries.definition: The plain plural that counts individual leaves; foliage never counts.
entries.definitionCN: 普通复数，一片一片地数；foliage 从不计数。

entries.definition: An English formation on leaf plus -age, close in sense but far rarer than foliage.
entries.definitionCN: 由 leaf 加 -age 的英语构词，意义接近，但远比 foliage 少见。

entries.definition: The whole upper layer of a tree or forest, branches included; foliage is the leaf part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指树或林的上层，含枝条；foliage 是其中的叶部。

entries.definition: Green plants as a pleasant sight; foliage is the leaf mass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 作为悦目景色的绿色植物；foliage 是叶丛本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root and the real horticultural terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁词根与真实园艺术语。

normal.en: Latin folium 'leaf' + -age (collective): a mass of leaves.
normal.cn: 拉丁 folium「叶」+ -age（集合）：成片的叶子。

normal.en: The family: foliar, foliate, defoliate, foliation.
normal.cn: 同族：foliar、foliate、defoliate、foliation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: dense foliage, autumn foliage, foliage plant, cut foliage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：茂密叶丛、秋叶、观叶植物、切叶。

normal.en: The same root gives folio and portfolio, both about sheets of paper.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 folio 与 portfolio，都与纸页有关。

normal.en: Florists sell cut foliage as material, the same way nurseries sell foliage plants.
normal.cn: 花艺师把切叶当材料卖，苗圃则卖观叶植物。

abstract.en: Picture one green surface spread over a whole wood, with no single leaf visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片森林上铺着一张绿表面，看不到单独一片叶。

abstract.en: Picture autumn as a painter repainting that surface from green to copper.
abstract.cn: 想象秋天是一位画家，把那层表面从绿改涂成铜色。

abstract.en: Picture a page and a leaf sharing one word because both are thin and flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸与一片叶共用一个词，因为两者都薄而平。

examples.en: The hedge keeps its foliage through the coldest months.
examples.cn: 这道树篱在最冷的几个月里仍保留叶丛。

examples.en: Cut foliage is sold by weight at the flower market.
examples.cn: 切叶在花市按重量出售。

examples.en: Acid rain damaged the foliage of the upland forest.
examples.cn: 酸雨损害了高地森林的叶丛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛利（foli）叶 + 集合（age）」——一大团叶子 → 叶丛；叶子总称

root: 古法语 feuillage 来自 feuille「叶」，再往前是拉丁 folium「叶」；folium 与希腊 phyllon 的联系一般认为成立，更深词根未定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat leaves as one mass, then as shade, colour, cut material, fodder, ornament, a plant class and finally a hiding place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都先把叶子当成一团，再依次当作阴影、颜色、切材、饲料、纹样、植物类别，最后当作藏身之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous green surface made of countless leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：由无数叶片连成的一整张绿色表面。

branches.en: MASS INTO LAYER: a crowd of leaves becomes a canopy with depth.
branches.cn: 成团成层：一堆叶子变成有厚度的一层。

branches.en: COLOUR: the same mass is valued as paint on a landscape.
branches.cn: 颜色：同一团叶被当作风景上的颜料。

branches.en: MATERIAL: cut for the vase or browsed by animals, leaves become stock or feed.
branches.cn: 材料：剪进花瓶或被牲畜啃食，叶子成了货品或饲料。

branches.en: PATTERN AND CLASS: art keeps the outline, horticulture keeps the label.
branches.cn: 纹样与类别：艺术保留轮廓，园艺保留标签。

branches.en: COVER: thick enough to hide a nest, the mass becomes a place.
branches.cn: 掩蔽：厚到能藏巢，这团叶就成了一个地方。

intro.en: Foliage is Latin folium plus a French collective suffix; the root also builds the vocabulary of pages and of defoliation.
intro.cn: foliage 是拉丁 folium 加法语集合后缀；这个词根还构成纸页与落叶方面的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin folium 'leaf' gives folia, foliaris and foliatus; -age marks a collective mass in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 folium「叶」给出 folia、foliaris 与 foliatus；-age 在法语中表示集合。

items.example: The root names the flat green organ.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指扁平的绿色器官。

items.example: The plural was felt as a mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数带有集合意味。

items.example: It turns a single leaf into a mass.
A foliated capital shows carved leaves.
items.exampleCN: 有叶饰的柱头刻着叶子。

definition_zh: 叶子；书页；薄片；（桌子的）活动板；翻（书）
definition_en: the flat green part of a plant; a sheet of paper or a thin sheet of metal; a hinged board that extends a table; to turn pages
core_image: 一片扁平的绿色薄片从茎上伸出，把阳光摊开接住
scene: 正午的强光直射下来，这片叶子慢慢调整角度，把光线错开。A single leaf turns toward the light.
sceneCN: 这里 leaf 指「植物进行光合的扁平器官」（第 1 个义项：植物的叶）；句意为一片叶子朝光转动。

pos.zh: 叶；叶子
（书）页；薄片；活动桌板
翻（书页）；长叶

senses.title: The flat green organ of a plant
senses.titleCN: 植物进行光合的扁平器官
senses.definition: the flat, usually green organ in which a plant captures light
senses.definitionCN: 植物捕获光能的扁平器官，通常为绿色
senses.example: A single leaf turns toward the light.
senses.exampleCN: 一片叶子朝光转动。
senses.why: Leaf comes from Old English leaf, a word for the blade of a plant, and the whole plant world is built on that one flat shape.
senses.whyCN: leaf 来自古英语，指植物的扁片；整个植物界都建立在这一个扁平形状上。

senses.title: A sheet in a book
senses.titleCN: 书里的一张纸
senses.definition: one sheet of a book, with its two sides
senses.definitionCN: 书中一张纸，含正反两面
senses.example: She tore a leaf from the notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 她从笔记本上撕下一张纸。
senses.why: A page is thin, flat and turns over, so the plant word was borrowed for paper, and both still 'turn'.
senses.whyCN: 纸页薄、平、会翻，于是植物的词被借去指纸，两者至今都「翻」。

senses.title: A very thin sheet of metal
senses.titleCN: 极薄的金属片
senses.definition: a thin sheet of metal, as gold leaf used in gilding
senses.definitionCN: 极薄的金属片，如贴金用的金箔
senses.example: The dome was finished with gold leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 穹顶最后贴上了金箔。
senses.why: Metal beaten thin enough to flutter behaves like a leaf, and crafts adopted the plant name.
senses.whyCN: 金属被打薄到能飘动，举止就像叶子，手艺行当于是采用了这个植物名。

senses.title: A hinged board on a table
senses.titleCN: 桌面上可翻起或抽出的板
senses.definition: a board hinged or sliding in a table to extend its top
senses.definitionCN: 桌面上铰接或滑动以加长桌面的板
senses.example: Pull out the leaf to seat six.
senses.exampleCN: 把活动板拉出来就能坐六个人。
senses.why: The board opens like a leaf unfolding, so furniture makers kept the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这块板打开时像叶子展开，家具匠于是沿用同一个词。

senses.title: Tea or tobacco leaf
senses.titleCN: 茶叶或烟叶
senses.definition: the dried leaf of tea or tobacco as a product
senses.definitionCN: 作为产品的茶叶或烟叶
senses.example: The tea leaf is rolled before drying.
senses.exampleCN: 茶叶在烘干前要揉捻。
senses.why: Trade names the product by the organ harvested, so whole industries speak of leaf.
senses.whyCN: 行业按采收的器官给产品命名，于是整个行业都说「叶」。

senses.title: To turn pages quickly
senses.titleCN: 快速翻看
senses.definition: to turn pages, especially quickly or casually
senses.definitionCN: 翻动书页，尤指快速地翻
senses.example: He leafed through the report before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前他把报告翻了一遍。
senses.why: The verb comes from the noun for a page: moving a page is moving a leaf.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自指纸页的名词：动一页就是动一片叶。

senses.title: To turn over a new leaf
senses.titleCN: 重新做人、重新开始
senses.definition: to begin behaving better after a period of bad behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在不良行为之后开始好好做
senses.example: She turned over a new leaf after the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 受到警告后她改过自新。
senses.why: In an old book a leaf is a page, so turning one over means starting a fresh side of the record.
senses.whyCN: 在旧时的书里，leaf 就是一页，翻过去意味着从记录的另一面重新开始。

senses.title: A leaf-like part or scale
senses.titleCN: 植物体上叶状的部位或鳞片
senses.definition: a leaf-like structure or scale, as in a moss or a bulb
senses.definitionCN: 苔类或鳞茎上的叶状结构或鳞片
senses.example: Each bulb leaf stores food through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 每片鳞叶整个冬天都在贮藏养分。
senses.why: Botany extends the word to any flat lateral organ, because function follows form rather than strict identity.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个词扩展到任何扁平的侧生器官，因为功能跟着形状走，而不拘于严格同一性。

intro.en: Leaf is native English, from Old English leaf, from Germanic laub; a link to Latin folium is sometimes suggested but not established.
intro.cn: leaf 是英语本族词，来自古英语 leaf，再往前是日耳曼语的 laub；有人提出它与拉丁 folium 有联系，但未获证实。

items.en: Old English leaf meant 'leaf' and also 'sheet of paper', so the page sense is as old as the word in English.
items.cn: 古英语 leaf 既指「叶」，也指「纸页」，可见纸页义在英语中与这个词一样古老。

items.en: The Germanic form laub is behind German Laub 'foliage' and English leaf; the family is well attested.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 laub 是德语 Laub「叶丛」与英语 leaf 的来源，这个词族有充分书证。

items.en: A pre-Germanic form such as leubh- 'leaf, peel' is sometimes given, but it is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 有时给出 leubh-「叶、剥皮」这类前日耳曼形式，但那是重构，不是有书证词。

items.en: Because a page is a leaf, English kept leaf for paper long after French page entered the language.
items.cn: 因为一页就是一片叶，法语 page 进入英语后，leaf 仍长期保留纸页义。

items.en: Gilders and cabinetmakers extended the word to thin metal and to hinged boards, both flat and leaf-like.
items.cn: 贴金匠与家具匠把它扩展到薄金属与铰接板，两者都扁而像叶。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the suggested link between Germanic laub and Latin folium is a hypothesis; no common ancestor has been demonstrated, so any such form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：日耳曼 laub 与拉丁 folium 的联系只是假说，尚未证明共同祖形，凡给出的此类形式都是重构。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that are unrelated in root from true relatives; group two holds leaf words by shape.
note.cn: 第一组区分词根无关的外形相近词与真正的同族词；第二组按形状列出各类「叶」。

entries.definition: From Old English laefan 'to allow, leave behind', a verb, not a plant word at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 laefan「准许、留下」，是动词，与植物无关。

entries.definition: From be- plus lief 'dear', from a root meaning 'to love'; only the ending looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 be- 加 lief「亲爱的」，词根意为「爱」，只有词尾相像。

entries.definition: Leaf plus the diminutive -let: a small leaf or a single sheet of printed matter.
entries.definitionCN: leaf 加小称后缀 -let：小叶，或单张印刷品。

entries.definition: From Old English hlaf 'bread'; the shape is similar, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 hlaf「面包」；形状相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: The leaf of a grass, long and narrow; leaf is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指禾草的叶，长而窄；leaf 是通称。

entries.definition: The leaf of a fern or palm, large and divided; it is a special case of a leaf.
entries.definitionCN: 指蕨或棕榈的叶，大而分裂，是叶的一种特例。

entries.definition: The narrow leaf of a pine or fir; again a shape-specific leaf.
entries.definitionCN: 指松杉的针状叶，同样是按形状特指的叶。

entries.definition: The leaves of a plant as one mass; leaf counts a single blade.
entries.definitionCN: 把一株植物的叶当作一团；leaf 数的是单片。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the native root, the real compounds and the real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用本族词根、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: Old English leaf meant both 'leaf' and 'page', which is why a book has leaves.
normal.cn: 古英语 leaf 既指叶也指纸页，所以书有「叶」。

normal.en: The family: leafy, leaflet, leafless, leafed.
normal.cn: 同族：leafy、leaflet、leafless、leafed。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fallen leaves, leaf through, gold leaf, leaf litter.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：落叶、翻阅、金箔、落叶层。

normal.en: The idiom turn over a new leaf comes from turning to a fresh page.
normal.cn: 习语「翻过新的一页」来自翻到崭新的一页。

normal.en: The verb leafs, leafed, leafing is regular, unlike the noun plural leaves.
normal.cn: 动词 leafs、leafed、leafing 是规则的，与名词复数 leaves 不同。

abstract.en: Picture a table opening like a flower when the extra board slides out.
abstract.cn: 想象多出的板滑出时，桌子像花一样打开。

abstract.en: Picture a record with two sides, and you decide to start on the clean one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张两面都有记录的纸，你决定从干净的那面重新开始。

abstract.en: Picture a bulb as a stack of thick leaves waiting underground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个鳞茎是地下叠着的一摞厚叶。

examples.en: A fallen leaf floated down the gutter.
examples.cn: 一片落叶顺排水沟漂下去。

examples.en: He leafed through the atlas while he waited.
examples.cn: 等的时候他翻着地图册。

examples.en: The frame is covered with gold leaf by hand.
examples.cn: 框子用手工贴上金箔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离（leaf）开的叶」——从枝上离开的薄片 → 叶子；书页

root: 古英语 leaf「叶、纸页」，来自日耳曼语 laub；与拉丁 folium 的联系仅为假说，未证明共同祖形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one shape, thin and flat: a plant organ, a page, a metal sheet, a table board, a traded product, and finally the acts of turning pages and starting afresh.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在同一个形状上——薄而平：植物器官、纸页、金属片、桌板、交易产品，最后是翻页与重新开始这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thin flat blade, made to catch light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄而平的叶，天生用来接住光。

branches.en: SHAPE FIRST: the plant organ and its leaf-like variants share the flat form.
branches.cn: 形状在先：植物器官与其叶状变体共享扁平形状。

branches.en: PAGE AND TURNING: a page is a leaf, so reading is leafing.
branches.cn: 纸页与翻动：一页就是一片叶，所以阅读就是翻叶。

branches.en: METAL: gold beaten thin behaves like a leaf.
branches.cn: 金属：金子打薄后举止像叶。

branches.en: FURNITURE: a board opens the way a leaf unfolds.
branches.cn: 家具：一块板像叶一样展开。

branches.en: PRODUCT AND IDIOM: harvested leaf becomes trade, and a turned page becomes a fresh start.
branches.cn: 产品与习语：采下的叶成为商品，翻过的一页成为新开始。

intro.en: Leaf is a native Germanic word, so it has no Latin affixes; its compounds are English through and through, and no Latin cognate can be relied on.
intro.cn: leaf 是日耳曼本族词，没有拉丁词缀；它的复合词纯属英语，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English leaf and Germanic laub supply the root; -y, -let and -less are native or Romance suffixes used on it, and no Latin cognate is established.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 leaf 与日耳曼 laub 提供词根；-y、-let、-less 是加在其上的后缀，拉丁同族词未获证实。

items.example: The word is native, not borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是本族词，不是借词。

items.example: German Laub preserves the old form.
items.exampleCN: 德语 Laub 保留了古老形式。
它把 leaf 变成 leafy。

items.example: A leafy hedge screened the door.
It makes leaflet, a small leaf.

items.meaning: a small leaf; a printed sheet

items.example: It makes leafless, bare of leaves.
A leafed stem rooted in water.
items.exampleCN: 一根带叶的茎在水里生根。

definition_zh: 多叶的；由叶组成的；叶菜类的；（街区）绿树成荫的
definition_en: having many leaves, made of leaves, or consisting mainly of edible leaves
core_image: 一根枝条叶片密到看不见茎，整条街被这层绿盖住
scene: 老城南边那条街两侧的梧桐把阳光筛成碎斑，中介带人看房时总要先提这一点。A leafy street like that sells houses faster than a bare one.
sceneCN: 这里 leafy 是「（街区）树木成荫的」（第 5 个义项：用多叶来形容一个地方绿荫浓密）；句意：那样绿树成荫的街道，房子卖得比光秃秃的街道快。

pos.zh: 多叶的；枝叶茂密的
由叶子组成的；叶制的
叶菜类的；以叶片为食用部分的
绿树成荫的（街道、郊区）

senses.title: Full of leaves
senses.titleCN: 多叶的：叶片盖满枝干
senses.definition: having many leaves; covered with leaves
senses.definitionCN: 多叶的；枝叶茂密的
senses.example: A leafy branch hung over the path.
senses.exampleCN: 一根多叶的枝条悬在小路上。
senses.why: The suffix -y in English adjectives means 'having the quality of', so leafy is simply leaf plus abundance.
senses.whyCN: 英语形容词后缀 -y 表示「具有……的性质」，leafy 就是叶加上「多」这一层。

senses.title: Made of leaves
senses.titleCN: 叶制的：拿叶子当材料
senses.definition: made of leaves or built from leaf material
senses.definitionCN: 由叶子制成的
senses.example: The nest is a leafy ball above the water.
senses.exampleCN: 巢是水面上方一个用叶子团成的球。
senses.why: Once a leaf stops being a living organ and becomes a material, the same adjective names the substance.
senses.whyCN: 一旦叶片不再是活器官而变成材料，同一个形容词就用来指这种材料。

senses.title: Leaf vegetables
senses.titleCN: 叶菜的：以叶片为食用部分
senses.definition: consisting mainly of edible leaves, as a class of vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 叶菜类的；以叶为食的
senses.example: Leafy greens lose vitamins if boiled too long.
senses.exampleCN: 叶菜煮得太久会损失维生素。
senses.why: Shops sort vegetables by the part that gets eaten; leafy names the group whose edible part is the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 商店按食用部位给蔬菜分堆；leafy 指可食部分为叶片的那一堆。

senses.title: Canopy layer
senses.titleCN: 叶层的：构成厚密林冠
senses.definition: of or forming a dense layer of leaves in a canopy
senses.definitionCN: 叶层厚密的；构成林冠叶层的
senses.example: The leafy canopy kept the ground cool.
senses.exampleCN: 茂密的树冠让地面保持凉爽。
senses.why: In ecology the leaves of a stand act as one layer, and leafy describes how thick that layer is.
senses.whyCN: 在生态学里，一片林木的叶子被当作一个层，leafy 描述这个层有多厚。

senses.title: Leafy neighbourhood
senses.titleCN: 绿荫的：街道两侧树木成行
senses.definition: having many trees and much greenery, used of streets and suburbs
senses.definitionCN: 绿树成荫的（街道、郊区）
senses.example: They bought a house in a leafy suburb.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在绿树成荫的郊区买了房子。
senses.why: Estate agents borrow the plant word to sell shade, quiet and clean air in a single adjective.
senses.whyCN: 房产中介借这个植物词，用一个形容词同时卖绿荫、安静与干净的空气。

senses.title: Vegetative shoot
senses.titleCN: 营养枝的：只长叶不开花
senses.definition: producing leaves rather than flowers or fruit
senses.definitionCN: 营养生长的；长叶而不开花的
senses.example: A leafy shoot grew from the cut stem.
senses.exampleCN: 一根营养枝从剪口处长了出来。
senses.why: Botany divides a shoot into leafy and flowering kinds; here leafy marks the phase, not the quantity.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把枝条分成营养枝与花枝；这里的 leafy 标的是阶段，不是数量。

senses.title: Whole-leaf tea
senses.titleCN: 全叶的：茶叶未经切碎
senses.definition: made of whole, unbroken leaves, used of tea
senses.definitionCN: 全叶的（茶叶未切碎）
senses.example: The tin holds a leafy tea from the high hills.
senses.exampleCN: 罐里装的是高山产的全叶茶。
senses.why: Tea grading counts how much leaf stays whole, so leafy turns into a quality label.
senses.whyCN: 茶叶分级看叶片保留得多完整，leafy 于是成了品质标签。

senses.title: Leaf-green
senses.titleCN: 叶绿的：像叶子那样的颜色
senses.definition: of a colour like that of leaves
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿色的
senses.example: She painted the wall a leafy green.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了叶绿色。
senses.why: Colour words often come from the object: leafy names the shade a leaf shows.
senses.whyCN: 颜色词常取自物体：leafy 指叶子呈现的那种色调。

senses.title: Leaf ornament
senses.titleCN: 叶饰的：建筑上刻成叶形
senses.definition: decorated with leaf-shaped forms, used of architecture
senses.definitionCN: 叶饰的（建筑装饰）
senses.example: The capital carries a leafy pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 柱头上有叶形花纹。
senses.why: Carvers copied leaves, and the adjective moved from the plant to the stone copy.
senses.whyCN: 雕刻匠照着叶子刻，形容词就从植物移到了石头的复制品上。

intro.en: Leafy is simply the native noun leaf plus the adjective suffix -y. The root is Germanic; the earliest date for the adjective is only approximate.
intro.cn: leafy 就是本族名词 leaf 加形容词后缀 -y。词根属日耳曼语；这个形容词的首见年代只是约数。

items.en: Old English leaf meant 'leaf' and also 'sheet of paper'; the noun has been in the language since the earliest records.
items.cn: 古英语 leaf 既指「叶」也指「纸页」，这个名词从最早的文献起就在英语里。

items.en: The Germanic form laub is attested in German Laub 'foliage' and in other Germanic languages, so the root itself is not in doubt.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 laub 有德语 Laub「叶丛」等书证，词根本身并无疑问。

items.en: The adjective suffix -y, from Old English -ig, means 'having the quality of' and is the same suffix as in sandy, salty and rainy.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -y 来自古英语 -ig，意为「具有……性质」，与 sandy、salty、rainy 里的后缀相同。

items.en: The adjective leafy appears in Middle English; the exact first written example is uncertain, since the form was common in dialect.
items.cn: 形容词 leafy 在中古英语时期已经出现；确切的首次书面用例不确定，因为该形式在方言中很常见。

items.en: Victorian gardening and later estate advertising extended leafy from plants to whole streets, and tea grading extended it to whole-leaf produce.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的园艺以及后来的房产广告，把 leafy 从植物扩展到整条街道；茶叶分级又把它扩展到全叶产品。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the root is securely Germanic, but any Indo-European ancestor offered for it is a reconstruction, and the link to Latin folium is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：词根确属日耳曼语，但凡为它给出的印欧祖形都是重构形式，与拉丁 folium 的联系只是假说。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share no root from the base word itself; group two holds words for thick green growth.
note.cn: 第一组区分词根无关的外形相近词与基础词本身；第二组列出表示浓密绿意的词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective; both have a long vowel, but leafy adds a final syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的名词；两者元音都长，但 leafy 多一个音节。

entries.definition: From leak, probably a Germanic word for 'drip'; nothing to do with plants.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 leak，大概是日耳曼语中表示「滴漏」的词，与植物无关。

entries.definition: From Old English lif 'existence'; the vowel is /aɪ/ and the spelling has no a.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 lif「生命」；元音是 /aɪ/，拼写里没有 a。

entries.definition: Leaf plus the privative -less: without leaves, the exact opposite of leafy.
entries.definitionCN: leaf 加否定后缀 -less：无叶的，正好与 leafy 相反。

entries.definition: Having thick, healthy growth, often of grass; leafy counts leaves, lush judges moisture.
entries.definitionCN: 指草木厚密、长势好，多用于草；leafy 数叶子，lush 判断水分是否充足。

entries.definition: Covered with green vegetation; a bookish word for the same look.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖着绿色植被；是形容同一种景象的书面词。

entries.definition: Having many branches close together; leafy is about leaves, bushy about the branching.
entries.definitionCN: 指枝条多而密；leafy 讲叶子，bushy 讲分枝。

entries.definition: The leaves of a plant taken as one mass; leafy says that mass is thick.
entries.definitionCN: 把一株植物的叶子当作一团；leafy 说这一团很厚。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix and the real family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的后缀与真实的词族，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: leaf + -y, the same suffix as in sandy and salty: full of what the noun names.
normal.cn: leaf 加 -y，与 sandy、salty 同一种后缀：充满名词所指的东西。

normal.en: The family: leaf, leaflet, leafless, leafage, leafed.
normal.cn: 同族：leaf、leaflet、leafless、leafage、leafed。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: leafy green, leafy suburb, leafy canopy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：绿叶菜、绿荫郊区、茂密树冠。

normal.en: Foliage is the mass; leafy says the mass is thick.
normal.cn: foliage 是那一团叶子；leafy 说这一团很厚。

normal.en: A supermarket shelf says leafy greens; an estate agent's window says leafy street.
normal.cn: 超市货架写的是叶菜，房产中介的橱窗写的是绿荫街道。

abstract.en: Picture a wall so covered in ivy that no brick shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一面被常春藤盖满、看不见砖的墙。

abstract.en: Picture a street where the trees meet overhead and the pavement is in shadow at noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，树冠在头顶合拢，正午路面仍在阴影里。

abstract.en: Picture one word that turns a plant part into a description of a whole neighbourhood.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词，把一个植物器官变成对整个街区的描述。

examples.en: A leafy branch hung over the path.
examples.cn: 一根多叶的枝条悬在小路上。

examples.en: They bought a house in a leafy suburb.
examples.cn: 他们在绿树成荫的郊区买了房子。

examples.en: Leafy greens lose vitamins if boiled too long.
examples.cn: 叶菜煮得太久会损失维生素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叶（leaf）加衣（y）」——给街道披上一层叶衣，就成了绿树成荫

root: 古英语 leaf「叶、纸页」＋形容词后缀 -y「充满……的」；日耳曼语 laub 有德语 Laub 等同族书证。更早的印欧形式属重构；与拉丁 folium 的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses spread outward from one idea: many leaves, then leaves as material, as food, as a layer, as shade, as a stage, as a grade, as a colour and as an ornament.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个意思向外铺开：叶子多，然后叶子成了材料、成了食物、成了一层覆盖、成了绿荫、成了生长阶段、成了等级、成了颜色、成了装饰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface so covered in leaves that the stem disappears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被叶子盖住、连茎都看不见的表面。

branches.en: ABUNDANCE: the suffix first says that leaves are present in quantity, then that they are the substance.
branches.cn: 多：后缀先说叶子数量多，再说叶子就是材料本身。

branches.en: FOOD: what is eaten is sorted by the plant part, and grades follow the same part.
branches.cn: 食物：可食部分决定分类，等级也按同一部位划分。

branches.en: LAYER: leaves of a stand or a shoot form one working layer in ecology and in botany.
branches.cn: 层：一片林木或一根枝条的叶子，在生态学与植物学里都构成一个工作层。

branches.en: PLACE: the layer becomes the character of a street, and the word sells shade.
branches.cn: 地点：这一层变成街道的性格，这个词开始卖绿荫。

branches.en: FORM: once leaves are a shape rather than a thing, they become a colour and a carved pattern.
branches.cn: 形状：当叶子不再是一样东西而是一个形状，它就变成一种颜色和一种雕花。

intro.en: Leafy is a native Germanic word with native suffixes; it has no Latin affixes and no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: leafy 是日耳曼本族词，配本族后缀；它没有拉丁词缀，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English leaf and Germanic laub supply the root; -y, -let, -less and -age are suffixes attached to it, and no Latin cognate is established.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 leaf 与日耳曼 laub 提供词根；-y、-let、-less、-age 是加在其上的后缀，拉丁同族词未获证实。

items.example: The word is native, not borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是本族词，不是借词。

items.example: German Laub preserves the old form.
items.exampleCN: 德语 Laub 保留了古老形式。
它把 leaf 变成 leafy。

items.example: A leafy hedge screened the door.
It makes leaflet, a small leaf.

items.meaning: a small leaf; a printed sheet

items.example: It makes leafless, bare of leaves.
It makes leafage, a mass of leaves.

definition_zh: 光合作用；绿色植物借光把二氧化碳和水合成糖并放出氧气的过程
definition_en: the process by which green plants and some other organisms use light to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar and oxygen
core_image: 叶片把阳光当针线，把空气里的碳和水缝成糖，顺手把氧气放出去
scene: 温室里的叶片颜色偏淡，研究员调整灯的高度，想知道补光强度够不够支撑整株生长。Light intensity sets the rate of photosynthesis in a leaf.
sceneCN: 这里 photosynthesis 指「绿色植物借光把二氧化碳和水合成糖并放出氧气的整个过程」（第 1 个义项：作为整体的光合作用）；句意：光照强度决定叶片光合作用的速率。

pos.zh: 光合作用（不可数，指整个过程）
（某类生物或某种条件下的）光合作用类型

senses.title: The whole process
senses.titleCN: 总过程：光、水、二氧化碳变成糖和氧
senses.definition: the complete process in which light energy is converted into chemical energy in plants
senses.definitionCN: 光合作用的总过程：光能被转成化学能
senses.example: The rate of photosynthesis rises with light intensity.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用的速率随光照强度上升。
senses.why: The word names one loop: light comes in, carbon and water go in, sugar and oxygen come out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一条闭环：光进来，碳和水进来，糖和氧出去。

senses.title: Light reactions
senses.titleCN: 光反应：水被拆开，能量被存起来
senses.definition: the light-dependent stage, in which water is split and energy is stored in carrier molecules
senses.definitionCN: 光反应阶段：水被分解，能量存进载体分子
senses.example: Photosynthesis begins with the light reactions in the thylakoid membranes.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用从类囊体膜上的光反应开始。
senses.why: The first half of the loop spends light; it splits water and charges the carriers that the second half will use.
senses.whyCN: 这条闭环的前半段花的是光：它拆开水，并给后半段要用的载体充电。

senses.title: Carbon fixation
senses.titleCN: 碳固定：把空气里的碳装进糖
senses.definition: the stage in which carbon dioxide is fixed into organic compounds
senses.definitionCN: 碳固定阶段：把二氧化碳固定成有机物
senses.example: Carbon fixation is the dark half of photosynthesis.
senses.exampleCN: 碳固定是光合作用中不直接依赖光的那一半。
senses.why: The second half of the loop builds: carbon from the air is attached to a skeleton and reduced into sugar.
senses.whyCN: 这条闭环的后半段负责建造：空气里的碳被接到骨架上，再被还原成糖。

senses.title: Rate
senses.titleCN: 速率：单位时间吸收多少碳
senses.definition: the measured rate at which a plant or a leaf carries out the process
senses.definitionCN: 光合速率：可测量的碳吸收量
senses.example: They measured photosynthesis with a gas exchange chamber.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用气体交换箱测定光合速率。
senses.why: Once the word names a process, instruments can put a number on it, and the word comes to mean that number.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词命名了一个过程，仪器就能给它一个数，这个词也随之指那个数。

senses.title: Underwater photosynthesis
senses.titleCN: 水下光合：沉水植物在水里做同一件事
senses.definition: the same process carried out by submerged aquatic plants and algae
senses.definitionCN: 沉水植物与藻类在水下进行的光合作用
senses.example: Underwater photosynthesis can be limited by dim light.
senses.exampleCN: 水下光合作用可能受弱光限制。
senses.why: The loop does not need air above the leaf; dissolved carbon and attenuated light are enough, so the word travels into water.
senses.whyCN: 这条闭环并不需要叶面上方的空气；溶解的碳和减弱的光就够了，于是这个词进入了水里。

senses.title: Oxygenic and anoxygenic
senses.titleCN: 产氧与不产氧：两种版本的光合
senses.definition: the process as carried out by organisms that release oxygen, or by those that do not
senses.definitionCN: 产氧光合作用与不产氧光合作用
senses.example: Oxygenic photosynthesis filled the early atmosphere with oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 产氧光合作用把早期大气填满了氧气。
senses.why: The same name covers two chemistries: one splits water and releases oxygen, the other uses other donors and releases none.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名字覆盖两套化学：一套拆水放氧，另一套用别的供体而不放氧。

senses.title: Artificial photosynthesis
senses.titleCN: 人工光合：用光驱动化学合成
senses.definition: a human-made system that uses light to make fuel or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 人工光合作用：人造系统用光制造燃料或化学品
senses.example: Artificial photosynthesis aims to store solar energy in fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 人工光合作用的目标是把太阳能存进燃料里。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the word because their device copies the loop: light in, chemical bonds out.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借这个词，是因为他们的装置复制了这条闭环：光进去，化学键出来。

senses.title: Gross primary production
senses.titleCN: 群落总初级生产：整片植被固定的碳
senses.definition: the total carbon fixed by a plant community, the sum of all its photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 群落总初级生产量：整片植被光合固定的碳总量
senses.example: Satellites estimate photosynthesis over the whole forest.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星估算整片森林的光合总量。
senses.why: Scale the loop from one leaf to a forest and the word becomes a budget line in the global carbon account.
senses.whyCN: 把这条闭环从一片叶放大到一片森林，这个词就成了全球碳账本上的一行预算。

intro.en: Photosynthesis is a nineteenth-century scientific compound of two Greek elements: light and a putting-together.
intro.cn: photosynthesis 是十九世纪的科学复合词，由两个希腊成分构成：光，以及「放在一起」。

items.en: Greek phos (phōs), phōtos meant 'light', and it supplies the first element in photology, photometer and photograph.
items.cn: 希腊语 phos（phōs）、phōtos 意为「光」，是 photology、photometer、photograph 的第一成分。

items.en: Greek synthesis meant 'a putting together', from syn- 'together' plus thesis 'a placing', from tithenai 'to put'.
items.cn: 希腊语 synthesis 意为「放在一起」，由 syn-「共同」加 thesis「放置」构成，后者来自 tithenai「放」。

items.en: The compound is generally credited to the American botanist Charles Reid Barnes, who proposed it in 1893 for the light-driven building of organic matter.
items.cn: 这个词一般归功于美国植物学家查尔斯·里德·巴恩斯，他在 1893 年为光驱动合成有机物这一过程提出了它。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word split into stages: the light reactions, the Calvin cycle, and later the Hill reaction and photophosphorylation.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，这个词分出了阶段：光反应、卡尔文循环，以及后来的希尔反应与光合磷酸化。

items.en: Since the 1970s artificial photosynthesis has named human-built cells that copy the loop, and satellite remote sensing has made the word a measurable global quantity.
items.cn: 1970 年代以来，人工光合成指人类制造、复制这条闭环的装置；卫星遥感又让这个词成了一个可测量的全球量。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the Greek roots are certain, but the exact year and first printed use of the English compound are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：希腊词根是确定的，但英语复合词的确切年份与首次印刷用例只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes built from the same pieces; group two holds the processes that are routinely confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组区分由相同部件拼出的形近词；第二组列出常与它混淆的过程。

entries.definition: The verb made from the noun with -ize: to carry out the process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词加 -ize 构成的动词：进行这一过程。

entries.definition: The adjective made with -ic: relating to or able to perform the process.
entries.definitionCN: 加 -ic 构成的形容词：与这一过程有关的，或能进行这一过程的。

entries.definition: The same Greek noun 'a putting together', but the first element is not light; it is a general word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出一个希腊名词「放在一起」，但第一成分不是光，而是一个通用词。

entries.definition: Light plus lysis 'a loosening': the light-driven splitting of water or another molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 光加 lysis「松开」：光驱动的水或其他分子分解。

entries.definition: The process that burns sugar and takes up oxygen; it runs the loop backwards.
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧糖、消耗氧气的过程；它是把这条闭环倒着走。

entries.definition: The same kind of building, powered by chemical reactions rather than light.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种建造，但动力来自化学反应而不是光。

entries.definition: A light-dependent reaction that consumes oxygen and releases carbon dioxide, wasting part of the gain.
entries.definitionCN: 一种依赖光的反应，消耗氧、放出二氧化碳，浪费掉一部分收益。

entries.definition: The loss of water vapour through leaf pores; it moves water, not carbon.
entries.definitionCN: 水汽经叶片小孔散失；它搬的是水，不是碳。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek pieces and the real stages, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊部件与真实阶段，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: photo- 'light' + synthesis 'a putting together': light is the tool that puts carbon and water together.
normal.cn: photo-「光」加 synthesis「放在一起」：光是用来把碳和水合在一起的工具。

normal.en: The two halves: light reactions then carbon fixation.
normal.cn: 前后两半：先光反应，再碳固定。

normal.en: The family: photosynthetic, photosynthesize, photosynthate, photosynthetically.
normal.cn: 同族：photosynthetic、photosynthesize、photosynthate、photosynthetically。

normal.en: Inputs and outputs in order: light, water, carbon dioxide in; sugar, oxygen out.
normal.cn: 输入输出按顺序记：光、水、二氧化碳进；糖、氧气出。

normal.en: A supermarket label for the same idea: nothing is eaten, everything is built from air and light.
normal.cn: 用一个超市标签记住同一件事：没有东西被吃掉，一切都由空气和光造出来。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf as a workshop that runs on sunlight and never buys raw material.
abstract.cn: 想象叶片是一间靠阳光运转、从不买原料的车间。

abstract.en: Picture the whole forest as one huge battery being charged by the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象整片森林是一块被太阳充电的巨大电池。
