abstract.en: Picture a chemist building a machine that does what a leaf does, only with pipes.
abstract.cn: 想象化学家造一台机器，用管道做叶子做的事。

examples.en: The rate of photosynthesis rises with light intensity.
examples.cn: 光合作用的速率随光照强度上升。

examples.en: Oxygenic photosynthesis filled the early atmosphere with oxygen.
examples.cn: 产氧光合作用把早期大气填满了氧气。

examples.en: Artificial photosynthesis aims to store solar energy in fuel.
examples.cn: 人工光合作用的目标是把太阳能存进燃料里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「光（photo）＋合成（synthesis）」——用光把碳和水合成糖

root: 希腊语 phōs「光」＋ synthesis「放在一起」（syn「共同」＋ thesis「放置」，出自 tithenai「放」）。词根清晰；英语复合词的确切首创年份只是约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loop: light is captured, water is split, carbon is fixed, sugar is built, oxygen is released, the rate is measured, the same loop runs under water or without oxygen, and finally it is scaled to a forest or copied in a factory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条闭环展开：捕获光、拆开水、固定碳、造出糖、放出氧、测出速率；同一条闭环也在水下或不产氧的条件下运行，最后被放大到整片森林，或被工厂复制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loop that takes light, air and water and returns sugar and oxygen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条吸入光、空气和水，产出糖和氧的闭环。

branches.en: THE LOOP: the word first names the whole circuit, not any one step.
branches.cn: 整环：这个词首先命名整个回路，而不是某一步。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: the circuit is taught as a light half and a carbon half.
branches.cn: 两半：教学上把回路分成依赖光的一半与固定碳的一半。

branches.en: MEASURE: once the circuit is a thing, a chamber can put a number on it.
branches.cn: 测量：回路一旦成为实体，气箱就能给它一个数。

branches.en: VARIANTS: the same circuit runs in water, and in some organisms without releasing oxygen.
branches.cn: 变体：同一条回路可以在水里运行，也可以在有些生物体内运行而不放氧。

branches.en: SCALE: the circuit is either copied in a factory or summed over a whole forest.
branches.cn: 尺度：这条回路要么在工厂里被复制，要么在整片森林上被加总。

intro.en: Photosynthesis is built from two Greek elements plus the Greek noun-forming suffix; no Latin word is involved.
intro.cn: photosynthesis 由两个希腊成分加希腊名词后缀构成，不涉及拉丁词。

latinIntro.en: Greek phōs 'light' and Greek synthesis 'a putting together' combine with -sis, the noun suffix of action; Latin supplies no counterpart in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 phōs「光」与希腊 synthesis「放在一起」与表示动作的名词后缀 -sis 组合；这一词族没有拉丁对应词。

items.example: It begins dozens of scientific words.
The bare stem carries only the idea of light.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的词干只带「光」这一概念。

items.example: It also appears in sympathy and synthesis.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 sympathy 与 synthesis 里。

items.example: The element names the act of putting.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分表示「放」这一动作。

items.example: It makes a noun of a process.
The word existed in Greek before the science.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在科学之前就存在于希腊语中。

items.example: The compound is a nineteenth-century coinage.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是十九世纪的新造词。

items.example: The adjective marks ability or relation.
items.exampleCN: 形容词标出能力或关联。

items.example: The verb turns the noun into an action.

definition_zh: 光合作用的；能进行光合作用的；由光合作用产生的
definition_en: relating to photosynthesis, or able to carry it out
core_image: 一片组织自带一套靠光吃饭的装置，灯一亮就开始干活
scene: 浅海岩面上那层紫色藻席并不捕食，太阳一出来就自己制造养分。Those photosynthetic mats survive on light alone.
sceneCN: 这里 photosynthetic 是「能进行光合作用的」（第 2 个义项：指生物或组织具有光合能力）；句意：那些能进行光合作用的藻席只靠光就能存活。

pos.zh: 光合作用的；与光合作用有关的
能进行光合作用的（生物、组织）
由光合作用产生的（氧气、糖）

forms.label: 副词（以光合作用的方式）

senses.title: Relating to the process
senses.titleCN: 总称：与光合作用有关的
senses.definition: relating to photosynthesis in general
senses.definitionCN: 与光合作用有关的
senses.example: The textbook opens with a photosynthetic diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 课本以一张光合作用的示意图开篇。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the process to a noun: a diagram, a measurement, a question about it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把这一过程挂到名词上：一张图、一次测量、一个关于它的问题。

senses.title: Able to carry it out
senses.titleCN: 能光合的：生物或组织具有这种能力
senses.definition: able to carry out photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 能进行光合作用的
senses.example: Those photosynthetic mats survive on light alone.
senses.exampleCN: 那些能进行光合作用的藻席只靠光就能存活。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks capacity: the organism has the machinery, whether or not it is running now.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词标的是能力：生物拥有这套装置，无论此刻是否在运转。

senses.title: Produced by it
senses.titleCN: 光合产出的：氧气、糖来自这个过程
senses.definition: produced by photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 由光合作用产生的
senses.example: The photosynthetic oxygen rose in bubbles.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用产生的氧气随气泡升上来。
senses.why: The same ending can point to the output rather than the maker: what the process gives off.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾也可以指向产物而不是执行者：这个过程放出来的东西。

senses.title: Photosynthetic nutrition
senses.titleCN: 光合营养的：靠光造食这种营养方式
senses.definition: describing a mode of nutrition in which food is built from light
senses.definitionCN: 光合营养的；以光合方式自养的
senses.example: Photosynthetic nutrition keeps the cell independent of prey.
senses.exampleCN: 光合营养让细胞不必依赖捕食。
senses.why: Nutrition is classified by the energy source, and this adjective names the light-powered class.
senses.whyCN: 营养方式按能量来源分类，这个形容词命名靠光的那一类。

senses.title: Pigment-bearing
senses.titleCN: 含光合色素的：组织里带着捕光色素
senses.definition: containing the pigments that capture light for the process
senses.definitionCN: 含光合色素的
senses.example: The photosynthetic layer sits just under the upper skin.
senses.exampleCN: 含光合色素的那一层就在上表皮之下。
senses.why: In anatomy the adjective marks the tissue where the pigments and the machinery are packed.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学里，这个形容词标出色素与装置密集分布的那层组织。

senses.title: High-activity
senses.titleCN: 光合活性强的：速率高、出力足
senses.definition: having a high rate of photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 光合活性强的；光合速率高的
senses.example: Young leaves are more photosynthetic than old ones.
senses.exampleCN: 幼叶的光合活性比老叶强。
senses.why: Comparatives turn the adjective into a ranking of output, so a leaf can be more or less photosynthetic than another.
senses.whyCN: 比较级让这个形容词变成产出的排序，于是叶片之间可以比谁的光合更强。

senses.title: Photoautotrophic
senses.titleCN: 光合自养的：生态类群的标签
senses.definition: belonging to the group that lives on light and inorganic carbon
senses.definitionCN: 光合自养的（生态类群）
senses.example: Photosynthetic organisms anchor almost every food web.
senses.exampleCN: 光合生物几乎支撑着每一条食物网。
senses.why: Ecology needs a label for the producers, and this adjective supplies it without naming a species.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要一个标签指称生产者，这个形容词不必点出物种就能做到。

senses.title: Light-driven, by analogy
senses.titleCN: 仿生的：材料或装置借光驱动
senses.definition: used by analogy of materials or devices driven by light
senses.definitionCN: （仿生用法）光驱动的；借光工作的
senses.example: The team built a photosynthetic film that splits water.
senses.exampleCN: 团队做出了一种能分解水的光驱动薄膜。
senses.why: When engineers borrow the adjective, they keep the input and the output and drop the plant.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借这个形容词时，保留输入与输出，去掉植物。

intro.en: Photosynthetic is the adjective of photosynthesis, made with the Greek-derived suffix -ic; the base word is a nineteenth-century scientific coinage.
intro.cn: photosynthetic 是 photosynthesis 的形容词，用希腊来源的后缀 -ic 构成；基础词是十九世纪的科学新造词。

items.en: Greek phōs 'light' supplies the first element, as in photograph and photometer.
items.cn: 希腊 phōs「光」提供第一成分，如 photograph 与 photometer。

items.en: Greek synthesis 'a putting together' comes from syn- 'together' and thesis 'a placing'.
items.cn: 希腊 synthesis「放在一起」来自 syn-「共同」与 thesis「放置」。

items.en: The noun photosynthesis was proposed in 1893, and the adjective followed as soon as the noun needed one.
items.cn: 名词 photosynthesis 于 1893 年被提出，名词一需要形容词，photosynthetic 就跟着出现。

items.en: The suffix -ic, from Greek -ikos through Latin -icus, means 'belonging to, of the nature of'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 经拉丁 -icus 来自希腊 -ikos，意为「属于……的、具有……性质的」。

items.en: Biochemistry fixed the adjective in phrases such as photosynthetic efficiency and photosynthetic pigment.
items.cn: 生物化学把这个形容词固定在 photosynthetic efficiency、photosynthetic pigment 这类短语里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the elements are clear, but the first printed use of the adjective is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：成分清楚，但这个形容词首次印刷使用的年份没有确切记载。

note.en: Group one separates the same-root family from look-alikes built with photo-; group two holds the nutrition labels that sit next to it.
note.cn: 第一组区分同族词与用 photo- 拼出的形近词；第二组列出与它相邻的营养方式标签。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective; the stress moves to the third syllable in the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的名词；变成形容词后重音移到第三音节。

entries.definition: The verb: to do the process, not merely to have the property.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：做这一过程，而不只是具备这种属性。

entries.definition: Light plus graph 'writing': relating to photography, with no carbon involved.
entries.definitionCN: 光加 graph「写」：与摄影有关，不涉及碳。

entries.definition: From synthesis without the light element: made by chemical combination, often artificial.
entries.definitionCN: 来自不含光成分的 synthesis：化学合成的，常指人造的。

entries.definition: Building food from chemical reactions instead of light; the same suffix, a different energy source.
entries.definitionCN: 靠化学反应而非光来造食；后缀相同，能量来源不同。

entries.definition: Living on light and inorganic carbon; a narrower ecological label.
entries.definitionCN: 靠光与无机碳生活；是更窄的生态标签。

entries.definition: Living on organic matter made by others; the opposite way of getting carbon.
entries.definitionCN: 靠别人制造的有机物生活；获取碳的反向方式。

entries.definition: Relating to splitting by light; one step inside the process, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与光致分解有关；是过程里的一步，不是全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix and the real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实后缀与真实复合词，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: photo- 'light' + synthesis + -ic: 'of the light-putting-together'.
normal.cn: photo-「光」加 synthesis 加 -ic：「属于把光放在一起这件事的」。

normal.en: The family: photosynthesis, photosynthesize, photosynthetically, photosynthate.
normal.cn: 同族：photosynthesis、photosynthesize、photosynthetically、photosynthate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: photosynthetic pigment, photosynthetic efficiency, photosynthetic bacteria.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：光合色素、光合效率、光合细菌。

normal.en: The -ic ending is the same one as in synthetic and photogenic.
normal.cn: -ic 结尾与 synthetic、photogenic 中的相同。

normal.en: Ability, product, or activity: the adjective can mark all three, and the noun tells you which.
normal.cn: 能力、产物或活动：这个形容词三者都能标，靠搭配的名词分辨。

abstract.en: Picture the sea floor lit from above, with a purple mat quietly making its own food.
abstract.cn: 想象被上方照亮的海底，一层紫色藻席安静地自制食物。

abstract.en: Picture a factory with no chimney for fuel, only a roof of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有燃料烟囱、只有玻璃屋顶的工厂。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a cell that says 'makes its own'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细胞身上贴着「自己造」的标签。

examples.en: Those photosynthetic mats survive on light alone.
examples.cn: 那些能进行光合作用的藻席只靠光就能存活。

examples.en: Young leaves are more photosynthetic than old ones.
examples.cn: 幼叶的光合活性比老叶强。

examples.en: Photosynthetic organisms anchor almost every food web.
examples.cn: 光合生物几乎支撑着每一条食物网。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「光（photo）＋合成（synthesis）＋的（-ic）」——能靠光自己造食的

root: 希腊 phōs「光」＋ synthesis「放在一起」＋形容词后缀 -ic（经拉丁 -icus 来自希腊 -ikos）。成分清楚，组合成词属十九世纪科学新造。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses are one adjective doing different jobs: pointing at the process, at the capacity, at the product, at the nutrition type, at the tissue, at the rate, at the ecological class, and finally at a human imitation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个形容词在干不同的活：指过程、指能力、指产物、指营养类型、指组织、指速率、指生态类群，最后指人类的仿制品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of tissue carrying its own light-powered factory.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块自带光驱动工厂的组织。

branches.en: POINTER: the adjective first just links a noun to the process.
branches.cn: 指向：这个形容词最初只是把名词与过程连起来。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND OUTPUT: the same ending can mark the machine or what the machine gives off.
branches.cn: 能力与产物：同一个词尾既能标机器，也能标机器放出的东西。

branches.en: CLASS: nutrition and ecology use the adjective as a category label.
branches.cn: 类别：营养学与生态学把它当作分类标签。

branches.en: TISSUE AND RATE: anatomy locates it, comparison ranks it.
branches.cn: 组织与速率：解剖学定位它，比较级给它排序。

branches.en: IMITATION: engineers keep the word and drop the plant.
branches.cn: 仿制：工程师留下这个词，去掉植物。

intro.en: Photosynthetic adds the Greek-derived suffix -ic to the noun photosynthesis; the whole family is Greek in origin, with no Latin source word.
intro.cn: photosynthetic 在名词 photosynthesis 上加希腊来源的后缀 -ic；整个词族源于希腊语，没有拉丁来源词。

latinIntro.en: Greek phōs, syn- and thesis build the noun; -ic, from Greek -ikos via Latin -icus, turns it into an adjective; no Latin base word exists for the family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 phōs、syn- 与 thesis 构成名词；-ic 经拉丁 -icus 来自希腊 -ikos，把它变成形容词；这一词族没有拉丁基础词。

items.exampleCN: 它开启许多科学复合词。

items.example: It also builds sympathy and synthesis.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 sympathy 与 synthesis。

items.example: The element comes from tithenai 'to put'.

items.exampleCN: 这个名词早于这门科学。

items.example: The base noun of the family.

items.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 进行光合作用；通过光合作用制造（有机物）
definition_en: to carry out photosynthesis, or to make something by means of it
core_image: 灯一亮，水草就开始冒泡，把光变成自己能吃的东西
scene: 水族箱的灯刚打开十分钟，草叶上就挂满细小的气泡，说明它们已经开始制造养分。The plants photosynthesize faster under the brighter lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 photosynthesize 指「进行光合作用」（第 1 个义项：作为不及物动词，表示植物在执行这一过程）；句意：在更亮的灯下，这些植物进行光合作用更快。

pos.zh: 进行光合作用
通过光合作用制造（有机物、氧气）
（微生物）以光合方式获取能量

collocations.zh: 通过光合作用把碳变成糖

senses.title: Carry out the process
senses.titleCN: 进行光合：植物在光下开工
senses.definition: to carry out photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 进行光合作用
senses.example: The plants photosynthesize faster under the brighter lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 在更亮的灯下，这些植物进行光合作用更快。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into an activity: the machinery is running, not merely present.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是名词变成的活动：装置正在运转，而不只是存在。

senses.title: Make by means of it
senses.titleCN: 光合生成：把某种产物造出来
senses.definition: to produce a substance by means of photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 通过光合作用生成（某种物质）
senses.example: The leaf photosynthesizes sugar from carbon dioxide and water.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片通过光合作用把二氧化碳和水生成糖。
senses.why: With an object, the verb names the output, and the process becomes a way of making something.
senses.whyCN: 带上宾语时，动词命名产物，这个过程就成了制造某物的方式。

senses.title: Fix carbon in light
senses.titleCN: 光下固碳：把空气里的碳收进体内
senses.definition: to fix carbon dioxide into organic form while light is available
senses.definitionCN: 在光下固定二氧化碳
senses.example: The cells photosynthesize only while the sun is up.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞只在有太阳时固定碳。
senses.why: Carbon fixation is the inward half of the act; the verb can profile just that gain.
senses.whyCN: 碳固定是这一动作向内的一半；动词可以只突出这份收获。

senses.title: Algal and bacterial
senses.titleCN: 藻与菌的光合：在水里或厌氧处进行
senses.definition: to perform the process as algae or photosynthetic bacteria do
senses.definitionCN: 藻类或光合细菌进行光合作用
senses.example: The mat photosynthesizes even in dim light.
senses.exampleCN: 这层藻席在弱光下也能进行光合作用。
senses.why: The verb does not belong to higher plants alone; any organism with the machinery can be its subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词不只属于高等植物；任何具备这套装置的生物都能做它的主语。

senses.title: Synthesize in the lab
senses.titleCN: 实验室里用光合成
senses.definition: to make a compound in the laboratory using light as the energy source
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室用光合成（化合物）
senses.example: The team photosynthesized the pigment in a flow cell.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在流动池里用光合成了这种色素。
senses.why: Chemists borrow the verb when their apparatus copies the leaf: light in, bonds made.
senses.whyCN: 当化学家的装置复制叶片时，他们借用了这个动词：光进去，键生成。

senses.title: Cause to be made
senses.titleCN: 使经光合而生成（及物）
senses.definition: to cause something to be produced through photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 使……经光合作用产生
senses.example: The coral photosynthesizes food with the algae inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚借体内的藻类通过光合作用生成食物。
senses.why: A host can be the subject even when another organism does the work, because the gain belongs to the host.
senses.whyCN: 即使干活的是另一种生物，宿主也能作主语，因为收益归宿主。

senses.title: Turn light into resource
senses.titleCN: 比喻：把外部能量换成可用之物
senses.definition: used by analogy of converting an external supply of energy into something usable
senses.definitionCN: （比喻）把外部能量转化为可用资源
senses.example: A good team photosynthesizes criticism into better work.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好的团队会把批评转化为更好的作品。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape of the loop: an outside supply is absorbed and rebuilt into something the organism can use.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留闭环的形状：外部供给被吸收，再造成生物能用的东西。

senses.title: Be capable of it
senses.titleCN: 具有光合能力：能长期处于这种状态
senses.definition: to be capable of carrying out the process, as a lasting property
senses.definitionCN: 具有进行光合作用的能力
senses.example: These deep-water algae photosynthesize at very low light.
senses.exampleCN: 这些深水藻类在极弱光下仍有光合能力。
senses.why: With a frequency or a place, the verb describes a standing capacity rather than one event.
senses.whyCN: 带上频率或地点时，这个动词描述的是一种长期能力，而不是一次事件。

intro.en: Photosynthesize is a back-formation from photosynthesis, made by replacing the noun ending with the verb suffix -ize.
intro.cn: photosynthesize 是从 photosynthesis 逆构而成的动词，把名词词尾换成了动词后缀 -ize。

items.en: Greek phōs 'light' is the first element, as in photograph and photometer.
items.cn: 希腊 phōs「光」是第一成分，如 photograph 与 photometer。

items.en: Greek synthesis 'a putting together' comes from syn- 'together' and thesis 'a placing'.
items.cn: 希腊 synthesis「放在一起」来自 syn-「共同」与 thesis「放置」。

items.en: The noun was proposed in 1893; the verb was formed later, as soon as writers needed to say that an organism performs the process.
items.cn: 名词于 1893 年被提出；动词形成较晚，是写作者需要说「某生物执行这一过程」时才有的。

items.en: The suffix -ize, from Greek -izein through Latin -izare, makes verbs meaning 'to act in the manner of' or 'to make'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ize 经拉丁 -izare 来自希腊 -izein，构成意为「以……方式行事」或「使……」的动词。

items.en: British spelling prefers -ise in many words, so photosynthesise is a spelling variant, not a different word.
items.cn: 英式拼写在许多词中偏好 -ise，所以 photosynthesise 只是拼写变体，不是另一个词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the elements and the pattern are clear, but no exact date is recorded for the first use of the verb.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：成分与构词方式清楚，但这个动词首次使用的确切年代没有记载。

note.en: Group one separates the same-root family and its spelling variants; group two holds verbs of gas exchange that are often swapped in.
note.cn: 第一组区分同族词与拼写变体；第二组列出常被混用的气体交换动词。

entries.definition: The noun: the process itself, not the act of performing it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：过程本身，而不是执行它的动作。

entries.definition: The -ise spelling used in British English; pronunciation and meaning are identical.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语使用的 -ise 拼写；读音与意义完全相同。

entries.definition: To make by combining, without any light: the chemist's general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 通过组合来制造，与光无关：化学家的通用动词。

entries.definition: Light plus copy: to reproduce a page, a completely different action.
entries.definitionCN: 光加 copy：复制纸页，是完全不同的动作。

entries.definition: To exchange gases while burning sugar; the loop run backwards.
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧糖的同时交换气体；把这条闭环倒着走。

entries.definition: To lose water vapour through the leaf; it moves water, not carbon.
entries.definitionCN: 经叶片散失水汽；搬的是水，不是碳。

entries.definition: To take in and build a substance into the organism; the general verb behind the specific one.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收并把物质建进生物体；这是具体动词背后的通用动词。

entries.definition: To build food from chemical reactions instead of light.
entries.definitionCN: 靠化学反应而非光来造食。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix and the real family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实后缀与真实词族，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: photosynthesis + -ize: to do what the noun names.
normal.cn: photosynthesis 加 -ize：做名词所指的那件事。

normal.en: The family: photosynthesis, photosynthetic, photosynthetically, photosynthate.
normal.cn: 同族：photosynthesis、photosynthetic、photosynthetically、photosynthate。

normal.en: The spelling pair: -ize in American English, -ise in British English.
normal.cn: 拼写成对记：美式用 -ize，英式用 -ise。

normal.en: Subjects can be leaves, algae, bacteria, even a coral host.
normal.cn: 主语可以是叶片、藻类、细菌，甚至珊瑚宿主。

normal.en: The metaphor works because the shape is the same: outside supply in, usable product out.
normal.cn: 比喻成立是因为形状相同：外部供给进，可用产物出。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switching on and bubbles appearing on every leaf at once.
abstract.cn: 想象灯一开，每片叶子上同时冒出气泡。

abstract.en: Picture a factory that runs only while the sun is above the roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一座只在太阳高过屋顶时才开工的工厂。

abstract.en: Picture a team that turns harsh words into a better design.
abstract.cn: 想象一个团队把刺耳的话变成更好的设计。

examples.en: The plants photosynthesize faster under the brighter lamp.
examples.cn: 在更亮的灯下，这些植物进行光合作用更快。

examples.en: The leaf photosynthesizes sugar from carbon dioxide and water.
examples.cn: 叶片通过光合作用把二氧化碳和水生成糖。

examples.en: The mat photosynthesizes even in dim light.
examples.cn: 这层藻席在弱光下也能进行光合作用。

root: 希腊 phōs「光」＋ synthesis「放在一起」＋动词后缀 -ize（经拉丁 -izare 来自希腊 -izein）。由名词逆构而成，成分清楚，动词首见年代无确切记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn one noun into an activity: running the process, making a product, fixing carbon, doing it as algae do, doing it in a lab, causing it in a host, borrowing it as a metaphor, and having the capacity at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把一个名词变成活动：执行过程、造出产物、固定碳、像藻类那样做、在实验室里做、让宿主获得产物、借作比喻、以及长期具备这种能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf switching on and turning light into food.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片叶开动起来，把光变成食物。

branches.en: ACT: the verb first says the machinery is running.
branches.cn: 动作：动词首先说装置正在运转。

branches.en: OUTPUT: with an object, the verb names what the process makes, even when a host owns the gain.
branches.cn: 产物：带宾语时，动词命名过程造出的东西，即使收益归宿主。

branches.en: CONDITION: light, or very little light, sets whether the act can happen at all.
branches.cn: 条件：光的多少决定这一动作能否发生。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES: algae and bacteria are subjects too.
branches.cn: 别的身体：藻类与细菌也能作主语。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE PLANT: a lab cell or a metaphor keeps the same shape.
branches.cn: 植物之外：实验室的装置或一个比喻，都保留同样的形状。

intro.en: Photosynthesize combines the Greek-built noun with the verb suffix -ize, itself Greek in origin through Latin.
intro.cn: photosynthesize 把希腊来源的名词与动词后缀 -ize 组合，后者经拉丁语也源于希腊语。

latinIntro.en: Greek phōs and synthesis build the noun; Greek -izein, through Latin -izare, supplies -ize; no Latin base word underlies the family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 phōs 与 synthesis 构成名词；希腊 -izein 经拉丁 -izare 提供 -ize；这一词族没有拉丁基础词。

items.exampleCN: 它开启许多科学复合词。
这个名词早于这门科学。

items.example: The base noun of the family.

items.meaning: to act in the manner of; to make
the same verb suffix in British spelling
items.meaningCN: 英式拼写中的同一动词后缀

items.example: The past tense marks a finished act.
items.exampleCN: 过去式标出已完成的动作。

items.meaning: in the middle of the act
items.exampleCN: 分词标出正在进行的动作。

definition_zh: 叶绿素；植物与藻类中捕获光能的绿色色素
definition_en: the green pigment in plants and algae that captures light for photosynthesis
core_image: 一层绿色染料铺在叶肉里，专门把红光和蓝紫光收进来
scene: 湖水的取样瓶过滤后颜色偏绿，绿色越深，说明水里的藻类越多。Chlorophyll readings tell how much algae is in the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 chlorophyll 是「叶绿素含量」（第 3 个义项：作为可以测定的浓度指标）；句意：叶绿素的测定值能说明湖里藻类有多少。

pos.zh: 叶绿素（不可数，指这种色素）
叶绿素分子；某一类叶绿素（可数）

derivatives.zh: 叶绿素衍生物（食品色素）

senses.title: The green pigment
senses.titleCN: 绿色素：把光收进来的染料
senses.definition: the green pigment found in plants and algae that absorbs light
senses.definitionCN: 植物与藻类中的绿色色素，负责吸收光
senses.example: Chlorophyll gives the leaf its colour.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素赋予叶片颜色。
senses.why: The word names a substance before it names anything else: a pigment, green, and sitting in the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先命名一种物质：一种绿色的、待在叶子里的色素。

senses.title: A molecular type
senses.titleCN: 分子类型：甲、乙等不同结构
senses.definition: one of several closely related pigment molecules, distinguished by small structural differences
senses.definitionCN: 几种结构相近的叶绿素分子之一（如甲、乙两种）
senses.example: The two main chlorophylls absorb slightly different wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 两种主要的叶绿素吸收的波长略有不同。
senses.why: Chemistry counts the variants, so the mass noun also has a plural for the distinct molecules.
senses.whyCN: 化学要数这些变体，于是这个不可数名词也有了指不同分子的复数。

senses.title: Measured content
senses.titleCN: 含量：单位面积或体积里有多少
senses.definition: the amount of the pigment present, measured as a concentration
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素含量：以浓度计的量
senses.example: Chlorophyll readings tell how much algae is in the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素的测定值能说明湖里藻类有多少。
senses.why: Once the pigment can be extracted and read, the word shifts from the substance to the number.
senses.whyCN: 色素一旦能被提取和读数，这个词就从物质转到了那个数。

senses.title: Fluorescence signal
senses.titleCN: 荧光：受光后发出的微弱红光
senses.definition: the faint red glow the pigment emits when excited, used as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素受激后发出的微弱红光，用作检测信号
senses.example: Chlorophyll fluorescence shows how hard the leaf is working.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素荧光显示叶片有多用力。
senses.why: The pigment absorbs light and can re-emit a little of it; instruments read that re-emission as a stress signal.
senses.whyCN: 色素吸收光，也能重新发出一点光；仪器把这点重新发出的光读成胁迫信号。

senses.title: Absorption bands
senses.titleCN: 吸收带：偏爱红光与蓝紫光
senses.definition: the particular wavelengths the pigment absorbs, mainly red and blue-violet
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素主要吸收红光与蓝紫光的波段
senses.example: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素吸收红光与蓝光，反射绿光。
senses.why: The colour we see is the light the pigment refuses; what it takes is the red and the blue-violet.
senses.whyCN: 我们看到的颜色是色素不要的光；它拿走的是红光与蓝紫光。

senses.title: Food colour
senses.titleCN: 食品色素：作为着色剂使用
senses.definition: the pigment used as a colouring agent in food or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 作为食品或药品着色剂的叶绿素
senses.example: Chlorophyll is listed as a green food colour.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素被列为一种绿色食品着色剂。
senses.why: Because it is green and edible, industry uses the substance as a dye rather than as a light catcher.
senses.whyCN: 因为它绿且可食，工业把它当染料用，而不是当捕光器。

senses.title: Derivative salts
senses.titleCN: 衍生物：铜钠盐等稳定形式
senses.definition: a stabilised derivative of the pigment, such as a copper salt, used commercially
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素的稳定衍生物，如铜钠盐
senses.example: The label lists chlorophyllin rather than chlorophyll.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上写的是叶绿素衍生物，而不是叶绿素。
senses.why: The natural pigment fades, so industry modifies it; the derivative keeps the green and loses the light work.
senses.whyCN: 天然色素会褪色，工业于是改造它；衍生物保住了绿色，却不再做捕光的工作。

senses.title: Porphyrin comparison
senses.titleCN: 卟啉对照：与血红素同一个环
senses.definition: the ring structure that the pigment shares with haem, differing in the central metal
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素与血红素共有的卟啉环结构，只在中位金属上不同
senses.example: Chlorophyll and haem share a ring, but one holds magnesium.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素与血红素共用一个环，只是其中一个装的是镁。
senses.why: Both molecules are built on a porphyrin ring; the central atom decides whether the result is green or red.
senses.whyCN: 两个分子都建在卟啉环上；中位原子决定结果偏绿还是偏红。

senses.title: Algal indicator
senses.titleCN: 水质指标：用含量判断藻华
senses.definition: the concentration used as an index of algal abundance in water
senses.definitionCN: 把叶绿素浓度当作水体藻类数量的指标
senses.example: High chlorophyll in summer points to an algal bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季叶绿素偏高说明发生了藻华。
senses.why: Water managers cannot count every cell, so they measure the pigment instead and let it stand for the algae.
senses.whyCN: 水质管理者数不清每一个细胞，于是改测色素，用色素代表藻类。

intro.en: Chlorophyll is a nineteenth-century scientific compound of two Greek words: pale green and leaf.
intro.cn: chlorophyll 是十九世纪的科学复合词，由两个希腊词构成：淡绿与叶。

items.en: Greek chlōros meant 'pale green, greenish-yellow', and it also names Chloris, the goddess of flowers.
items.cn: 希腊 chlōros 意为「淡绿、黄绿」，它也是花神克洛里斯名字的来源。

items.en: Greek phyllon meant 'leaf', and it builds words such as phyllotaxis, the arrangement of leaves.
items.cn: 希腊 phyllon 意为「叶」，它构成 phyllotaxis（叶序）这类词。

items.en: The pigment was named by the French chemists Pelletier and Caventou in 1818, after they isolated the green matter of leaves.
items.cn: 这种色素由法国化学家佩尔蒂埃与卡旺图在 1818 年分离出叶中绿色物质之后命名。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry showed that the pigment is a porphyrin ring with magnesium at its centre, close in structure to haem.
items.cn: 二十世纪的化学表明，这种色素是中心带镁的卟啉环，结构与血红素相近。

items.en: In the twentieth century the pigment and its copper derivative entered the food and pharmaceutical colour lists.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这种色素及其铜衍生物进入了食品与药品的着色剂清单。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the name is generally attributed to Pelletier and Caventou in 1818, but the exact manuscript date is approximate; the Greek roots are certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：命名一般认为出自佩尔蒂埃与卡旺图 1818 年的工作，但确切手稿年代只是约数；希腊词根是确定的。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes built with the same Greek pieces; group two holds the other leaf pigments.
note.cn: 第一组区分用相同希腊部件拼出的形近词；第二组列出叶片中的其他色素。

entries.definition: Green plus plastos 'formed': the organelle that holds the pigment, not the pigment itself.
entries.definitionCN: 绿加 plastos「成形」：装着这种色素的细胞器，而不是色素本身。

entries.definition: Green plus -osis: a condition in which leaves lose their green, from iron shortage.
entries.definitionCN: 绿加 -osis：叶片失绿的症状，常因缺铁。

entries.definition: The adjective: bearing chlorophyll, said of tissue or cells.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：含叶绿素的，用于组织或细胞。

entries.definition: Phyllon 'leaf' plus taxis 'arrangement': leaf order on a stem, with no pigment involved.
entries.definitionCN: phyllon「叶」加 taxis「排列」：茎上的叶序，与色素无关。

entries.definition: An orange-yellow pigment that also helps capture light; it passes energy to chlorophyll.
entries.definitionCN: 一种橙黄色色素，也参与捕光，并把能量传给叶绿素。

entries.definition: A water-soluble pigment making red and blue colours in leaves and fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 水溶性色素，使叶与果呈现红蓝色。

entries.definition: The oxygen-carrying blood protein; its haem group is a porphyrin ring like chlorophyll's.
entries.definitionCN: 运氧的血液蛋白；其血红素基团是与叶绿素相似的卟啉环。

entries.definition: Any substance that gives colour; chlorophyll is one pigment among many.
entries.definitionCN: 任何显色物质；叶绿素只是众多色素之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek pieces and the real chemistry, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用希腊部件与真实化学，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: chloro- 'pale green' + phyllon 'leaf': the green of the leaf.
normal.cn: chloro-「淡绿」加 phyllon「叶」：叶子的绿。

normal.en: The family: chlorophyllous, chlorophyllase, chlorophyllin, bacteriochlorophyll.
normal.cn: 同族：chlorophyllous、chlorophyllase、chlorophyllin、bacteriochlorophyll。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: chlorophyll content, chlorophyll fluorescence, total chlorophyll.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：叶绿素含量、叶绿素荧光、总叶绿素。

normal.en: One ring, two metals: magnesium makes it green, iron makes haem red.
normal.cn: 一个环，两种金属：装镁是绿的，装铁是红的。

normal.en: It absorbs red and blue and reflects green, which is exactly the colour we see.
normal.cn: 它吸收红与蓝、反射绿，而绿正是我们看到的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a thin green film laid over every cell of the leaf, catching light.
abstract.cn: 想象叶片每个细胞上都铺着一层极薄的绿膜，用来接光。

abstract.en: Picture a dye that keeps working as a dye long after it has stopped catching light.
abstract.cn: 想象一种染料，早已不再捕光，却仍当着染料。

abstract.en: Picture a lake whose greenness can be read as a number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个湖，它的绿可以被读成一个数。

examples.en: Chlorophyll gives the leaf its colour.
examples.cn: 叶绿素赋予叶片颜色。

examples.en: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
examples.cn: 叶绿素吸收红光与蓝光，反射绿光。

examples.en: High chlorophyll in summer points to an algal bloom.
examples.cn: 夏季叶绿素偏高说明发生了藻华。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绿（chloro）＋叶（phyll）」——让叶子发绿、替叶子接光的那种色素

root: 希腊 chlōros「淡绿、黄绿」＋ phyllon「叶」。词根清晰；命名者为佩尔蒂埃与卡旺图，1818 年，一般认为成立，确切手稿年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from substance to molecule to measurement to signal, then to its colour, its commercial forms, its chemical cousin, and finally its use as a water index.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从物质走到分子、测量、信号，再走到它的颜色、商品形式、化学近亲，最后走到作为水质指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green film spread through the leaf that takes in red and blue light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层铺在叶肉里、专收红光与蓝光的绿膜。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: the word begins as a name for a green stuff.
branches.cn: 物质：这个词最初是一种绿色东西的名字。

branches.en: COUNT: chemistry separates the variants and needs a plural.
branches.cn: 计数：化学分出变体，于是需要复数。

branches.en: READING: extracted or glowing, the pigment becomes a number or a signal.
branches.cn: 读数：被提取或被发光时，色素变成一个数或一个信号。

branches.en: OPTICS: what it takes and what it refuses explain its colour.
branches.cn: 光学：它拿什么、不要什么，解释了它的颜色。

branches.en: OUTSIDE: as dye, as derivative, as chemical cousin, as water index.
branches.cn: 叶外：作为染料、衍生物、化学近亲与水质指标。

intro.en: Chlorophyll is built from two Greek nouns; it has no Latin affixes and no Latin base word.
intro.cn: chlorophyll 由两个希腊名词构成；它没有拉丁词缀，也没有拉丁基础词。

latinIntro.en: Greek chlōros 'pale green' and phyllon 'leaf' combine directly; the family stays Greek, so no Latin entry applies.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 chlōros「淡绿」与 phyllon「叶」直接组合；这个词族保持希腊来源，没有适用的拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 它开启许多与绿色有关的词。

items.example: The bare stem carries only the colour.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的词干只带颜色义。

items.example: The noun names the organ, not the pigment.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名器官，不命名色素。
这个复合词于 1818 年造出。

items.example: The suffix names a prepared substance.

items.meaning: the bacterial form of the pigment
items.example: The prefix marks the bacterial source.

items.meaning: a loss of green in leaves
items.example: The medical suffix names a condition.
items.exampleCN: 医学后缀命名一种症状。

definition_zh: 叶绿体；植物与藻类细胞中进行光合作用的细胞器
definition_en: the organelle in plant and algal cells where photosynthesis takes place
core_image: 细胞里一间自带玻璃屋顶的小车间，装着色素和整条生产线
scene: 显微镜下的叶肉细胞像一间间小房间，每间里都挤着许多绿色的小颗粒。Each chloroplast runs its own sugar line inside the cell.
sceneCN: 这里 chloroplast 是「叶绿体这一细胞器」（第 1 个义项：作为细胞内的独立结构单位）；句意：每个叶绿体都在细胞里运行自己的一条造糖生产线。

pos.zh: 叶绿体（细胞器）
叶绿体的某一份拷贝（细胞内的一个个体）

senses.title: The organelle
senses.titleCN: 细胞器：细胞里干活的那一间
senses.definition: the organelle in plant and algal cells in which photosynthesis takes place
senses.definitionCN: 植物与藻类细胞中进行光合作用的细胞器
senses.example: Each chloroplast runs its own sugar line inside the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 每个叶绿体都在细胞里运行自己的一条造糖生产线。
senses.why: The word names a compartment: a body inside the cell with its own machinery and its own boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名一个隔间：细胞内一个有自己装置、有自己边界的身体。

senses.title: Its double membrane
senses.titleCN: 双层膜：两层边界把内外分开
senses.definition: the two membranes that enclose the organelle
senses.definitionCN: 包裹叶绿体的两层膜
senses.example: The chloroplast envelope has two membranes.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体的外被有两层膜。
senses.why: An organelle needs a wall; the double membrane is the evidence that it was once a separate cell.
senses.whyCN: 细胞器需要一层壁；双层膜正是它曾经是独立细胞的证据。

senses.title: Thylakoid stacks
senses.titleCN: 类囊体堆：膜叠成一个个小垛
senses.definition: the internal stack of thylakoid membranes where light is captured
senses.definitionCN: 内部叠成垛的类囊体膜，捕光就在这里
senses.example: The chloroplast packs its thylakoids into grana.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体把类囊体堆成基粒。
senses.why: Inside the compartment the membranes are folded into stacks, which is how a small space holds a large surface.
senses.whyCN: 隔间内部把膜折成垛，小空间于是装下了大表面。

senses.title: Its own genome
senses.titleCN: 自身基因组：环状脱氧核糖核酸
senses.definition: the small circular genome the organelle carries and expresses
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿体自带的环状基因组及其表达
senses.example: The chloroplast genome is inherited from the mother plant.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体基因组由母株遗传。
senses.why: A compartment with its own genes is a compartment with a history; the genome is the record of that past.
senses.whyCN: 一个有自己基因的隔间就是一段有历史的隔间；基因组是那段过去的记录。

senses.title: Endosymbiotic origin
senses.titleCN: 内共生起源：曾经是独立的蓝细菌
senses.definition: the organelle understood as a descendant of an engulfed photosynthetic bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 把叶绿体理解为被吞入的光合细菌的后代
senses.example: The chloroplast began as a free-living cyanobacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体最初是自由生活的蓝细菌。
senses.why: The double membrane and the circular genome both point one way: a host swallowed a cell and kept it.
senses.whyCN: 双层膜与环状基因组都指向同一件事：宿主吞下了一个细胞，并把它留下。

senses.title: Number and placement
senses.titleCN: 数量与分布：每个细胞里有几个、放在哪
senses.definition: the count and arrangement of the organelles within a cell
senses.definitionCN: 细胞内叶绿体的数目与位置
senses.example: A mesophyll cell may hold dozens of chloroplasts.
senses.exampleCN: 一个叶肉细胞可以容纳几十个叶绿体。
senses.why: Cells differ in how many they hold and where they sit, and the word counts those units.
senses.whyCN: 不同细胞装的数量与位置不同，这个词数的就是这些单位。

senses.title: Transformation
senses.titleCN: 叶绿体转化：把外源基因送进去
senses.definition: the genetic engineering of the organelle to express new genes
senses.definitionCN: 用基因工程让叶绿体表达新基因
senses.example: Chloroplast transformation avoids spreading genes through pollen.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体转化可避免基因随花粉扩散。
senses.why: Because the organelle has its own genome, engineers can edit it directly and keep the edit out of the pollen.
senses.whyCN: 因为细胞器有自己的基因组，工程师能直接编辑它，并让改动不进入花粉。

senses.title: Semi-autonomous organelle
senses.titleCN: 半自主细胞器：与线粒体同类
senses.definition: the organelle classed with mitochondria as semi-autonomous
senses.definitionCN: 与线粒体同属半自主细胞器
senses.example: Chloroplasts and mitochondria are both semi-autonomous.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体与线粒体都是半自主的。
senses.why: Two organelles share the same pattern: their own deoxyribonucleic acid, their own ribosomes, and a host that still controls them.
senses.whyCN: 两种细胞器共享同一套模式：自己的脱氧核糖核酸、自己的核糖体，以及仍然控制它们的宿主。

intro.en: Chloroplast is a nineteenth-century German scientific compound: green plus 'formed'.
intro.cn: chloroplast 是十九世纪德语的科学复合词：绿，加上「成形」。

items.en: Greek chlōros meant 'pale green', the same element that opens chlorophyll.
items.cn: 希腊 chlōros 意为「淡绿」，与 chlorophyll 的第一成分相同。

items.en: Greek plastos meant 'formed, moulded', from plassein 'to mould'; it also gives plastid and plastic.
items.cn: 希腊 plastos 意为「成形的、塑成的」，来自 plassein「塑造」；它也是 plastid 与 plastic 的来源。

items.en: The German botanist Eduard Strasburger is generally credited with the term in 1883, for the green bodies he saw in plant cells.
items.cn: 德国植物学家爱德华·施特拉斯布格一般认为在 1883 年提出了这个词，用来指他在植物细胞里看到的绿色体。

items.en: In the twentieth century the organelle was reinterpreted as a former cyanobacterium, an idea argued from its double membrane and circular genome.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这种细胞器被重新解释为以前的蓝细菌，依据是它的双层膜与环状基因组。

items.en: Late twentieth-century work made the organelle a target for transformation, because its genome is inherited maternally.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的工作使这种细胞器成为转化的目标，因为它的基因组由母方遗传。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the coinage is generally attributed to Strasburger in 1883, but the exact publication date is approximate; the Greek roots are certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：该术语一般认为由施特拉斯布格于 1883 年提出，但确切发表年代只是约数；希腊词根是确定的。

note.en: Group one separates the plastid family from look-alikes; group two holds the other organelles it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组区分质体家族与形近词；第二组列出常与它比较的其他细胞器。

entries.definition: The pigment inside the organelle; the two share chloro- but end differently.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞器里面的色素；两者共享 chloro-，但词尾不同。

entries.definition: Colour plus plastos: a pigment-bearing plastid that is not green.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色加 plastos：带色素而非绿色的质体。

entries.definition: White plus plastos: a colourless plastid used for storage.
entries.definitionCN: 白加 plastos：无色的、用于贮藏的质体。

entries.definition: The general class to which chloroplasts belong; every chloroplast is a plastid.
entries.definitionCN: 叶绿体所属的总类；每个叶绿体都是质体。

entries.definition: The other semi-autonomous organelle, which burns fuel instead of capturing light.
entries.definitionCN: 另一种半自主细胞器，烧燃料而不是捕光。

entries.definition: The membrane inside the chloroplast where light is captured.
entries.definitionCN: 叶绿体内部捕光的膜。

entries.definition: A stack of thylakoids; the chloroplast holds many grana.
entries.definitionCN: 类囊体叠成的垛；一个叶绿体含许多基粒。

entries.definition: Any specialised compartment of a cell; chloroplast is one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞内任何特化的隔间；叶绿体是其中一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek pieces and the real structure, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用希腊部件与真实结构，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: chloro- 'green' + plastos 'formed': the formed green body.
normal.cn: chloro-「绿」加 plastos「成形」：成形了的绿色体。

normal.en: The family: plastid, proplastid, chromoplast, leucoplast.
normal.cn: 同族：plastid、proplastid、chromoplast、leucoplast。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: chloroplast genome, chloroplast membrane, chloroplast transformation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：叶绿体基因组、叶绿体膜、叶绿体转化。

normal.en: Two membranes and a circular genome are the two clues to its past.
normal.cn: 双层膜与环状基因组是它过去身份的两条线索。

normal.en: Compare with the mitochondrion: one captures light, one burns fuel.
normal.cn: 与线粒体对照记：一个捕光，一个烧燃料。

abstract.en: Picture a cell as a building and each chloroplast as a workshop with its own roof.
abstract.cn: 想象细胞是一栋楼，每个叶绿体是一间自带屋顶的车间。

abstract.en: Picture a factory that kept the keys to its old independent address.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂，仍留着它旧日独立门牌的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of green membranes folded small enough to fit in a dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠绿膜折得极小，小到能装进一个点里。

examples.en: Each chloroplast runs its own sugar line inside the cell.
examples.cn: 每个叶绿体都在细胞里运行自己的一条造糖生产线。

examples.en: The chloroplast envelope has two membranes.
examples.cn: 叶绿体的外被有两层膜。

examples.en: Chloroplasts and mitochondria are both semi-autonomous.
examples.cn: 叶绿体与线粒体都是半自主的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绿（chloro）＋成形（plast）」——细胞里成形的一块绿色车间

root: 希腊 chlōros「淡绿」＋ plastos「成形的」（出自 plassein「塑造」）。词根清晰；术语由施特拉斯布格于 1883 年提出，一般认为成立，确切发表年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses build the organelle outward: the compartment, its two membranes, its folded stacks, its own genome, its bacterial past, its number in a cell, its use in engineering, and its class beside the mitochondrion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这间细胞器由内向外搭起来：隔间本身、两层膜、折叠的膜垛、自己的基因组、细菌般的过去、在细胞里的数量、在工程中的用途，以及与线粒体并列的类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a workshop inside the cell with its own roof, tools and blueprint.
core.cn: 核心意象：细胞里一间自带屋顶、工具与图纸的车间。

branches.en: BODY: the word names the compartment itself.
branches.cn: 实体：这个词命名隔间本身。

branches.en: SKIN AND SURFACE: two membranes wrap it, and folded membranes fill it.
branches.cn: 皮与面：两层膜包住它，折叠的膜填满它。

branches.en: HISTORY: its own genome and its double membrane both record a former free life.
branches.cn: 历史：自己的基因组与双层膜都记录了曾经的自由生活。

branches.en: COUNT: cells hold many, and the word counts those units.
branches.cn: 计数：细胞里有很多个，这个词数的就是这些单位。

branches.en: USE AND CLASS: engineers edit it, and biologists file it beside the mitochondrion.
branches.cn: 用途与类别：工程师编辑它，生物学家把它与线粒体归在一起。

intro.en: Chloroplast joins a Greek colour word to a Greek word for 'formed'; the family is Greek throughout.
intro.cn: chloroplast 把一个希腊颜色词与一个希腊语「成形」词连接；整个词族都是希腊来源。

latinIntro.en: Greek chlōros and plastos, with plassein 'to mould' behind the second element, build the word; no Latin base word applies.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 chlōros 与 plastos 构成这个词，后者背后是 plassein「塑造」；没有适用的拉丁基础词。

items.exampleCN: 这是 plastos 背后的动词。

items.meaning: a formed body in the cell

items.example: The prefix marks an earlier stage.
The first element is colour, not green.
items.exampleCN: 第一成分是颜色，不是绿。

items.meaning: an older name for the organelle

definition_zh: 气孔（复数）；叶片表皮上成对保卫细胞围成的小孔
definition_en: the small openings in the surface of a leaf, each guarded by two cells
core_image: 叶片背面一排排小嘴，天热时张开喘气，干旱时抿紧
scene: 把叶片背面撕下薄薄一层放到镜下，能看到成排的小孔整齐地嵌在细胞之间。The stomata open when the leaf needs to take in air.
sceneCN: 这里 stomata 是「叶片表皮上成排的小孔（复数总称）」（第 1 个义项：作为植物与外界交换气体的开口）；句意：叶片需要吸入空气时，这些气孔就张开。

pos.zh: 气孔（复数，植物叶表皮的气体交换开口）
（动物学）口；体表小孔（单数 stoma 的复数）

senses.title: Leaf openings
senses.titleCN: 叶片小孔：与外界交换气体的开口
senses.definition: the small openings in a leaf surface through which gases pass
senses.definitionCN: 叶片表面供气体进出的开口，复数总称
senses.example: The stomata open when the leaf needs to take in air.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片需要吸入空气时，这些气孔就张开。
senses.why: The plural is the ordinary form because a leaf never has just one; the word names the openings as a set.
senses.whyCN: 复数才是常用形式，因为一片叶从来不止一个孔；这个词把开口当作一整套来命名。

senses.title: The whole apparatus
senses.titleCN: 气孔器：孔加两个保卫细胞的整体
senses.definition: an opening together with the two guard cells that surround it
senses.definitionCN: 小孔连同围住它的两个保卫细胞所构成的整体
senses.example: Each stoma is a pair of guard cells with a gap between them.
senses.exampleCN: 每个气孔都是两个保卫细胞中间留一道缝。
senses.why: Botany treats the gap and the cells as one unit, and the plural covers many such units.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把缝隙与细胞当作一个单位，复数就指许多个这样的单位。

senses.title: Opening and closing
senses.titleCN: 开闭：孔口随条件张合
senses.definition: the opening and closing movement of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 气孔孔口的张开与闭合
senses.example: Stomata close when water is scarce.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水时气孔会闭合。
senses.why: A pore that can shut is a valve; the plural is often used for the behaviour of all the valves at once.
senses.whyCN: 能关闭的孔就是阀门；复数常用来指所有阀门一起表现出的行为。

senses.title: Density
senses.titleCN: 密度：单位叶面上有多少
senses.definition: the number of the openings per unit area of leaf surface
senses.definitionCN: 单位叶面积上的气孔数目
senses.example: Stomata density is higher on the lower surface.
senses.exampleCN: 下表面的气孔密度更高。
senses.why: Once the openings are countable, ecology uses their density as a trait of a species.
senses.whyCN: 开口一旦可数，生态学就把它们的密度当作物种性状。

senses.title: Conductance
senses.titleCN: 导度：水汽与气体通过的能力
senses.definition: the conductance of gases and water vapour through the openings
senses.definitionCN: 水汽与气体经这些开口传导的速率
senses.example: Stomata set the leaf's conductance to water vapour.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔决定叶片对水汽的导度。
senses.why: The openings are a resistance in a circuit of gas flow, and their collective conductance is what instruments report.
senses.whyCN: 这些开口是气体回路里的阻力，仪器报出的是它们总体的导度。

senses.title: Stomatal index
senses.titleCN: 气孔指数：与表皮细胞的比例
senses.definition: the ratio of the openings to the total number of epidermal cells
senses.definitionCN: 气孔数与表皮细胞总数的比例
senses.example: Stomata index is used to compare leaves of different sizes.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔指数用来比较大小不同的叶片。
senses.why: Counting alone is not enough when leaves differ in size, so the ratio normalises the count.
senses.whyCN: 叶片大小不同时，光数个数不够，于是用比例做归一化。

senses.title: Surface distribution
senses.titleCN: 分布：上表面与下表面的差别
senses.definition: the arrangement of the openings on the two leaf surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 气孔在上、下表面的分布格局
senses.example: Most stomata sit on the shaded lower surface.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数气孔位于背光的下表面。
senses.why: Placement follows light and water loss, and the plural names the whole pattern.
senses.whyCN: 位置取决于光照与失水，复数命名的是整个格局。

senses.title: Zoological pores
senses.titleCN: 动物学：口或体表小孔
senses.definition: openings or mouths in some animals, the plural of stoma in zoology
senses.definitionCN: 某些动物的口或体表小孔，动物学中 stoma 的复数
senses.example: The stomata of the worm open into a shared cavity.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蠕虫的口通入一个共同的腔。
senses.why: The same Greek word for 'mouth' was borrowed by zoology, so the plural has a second technical home.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词「口」被动物学借去，于是这个复数有了第二个术语归宿。

senses.title: Fossil leaf pores
senses.titleCN: 化石气孔：读古代大气的窗口
senses.definition: the openings preserved on fossil leaf surfaces, used to estimate past carbon dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 化石叶表面上保存下来的气孔，用来估算古代二氧化碳
senses.example: Fossil stomata hint at the air of the Cretaceous.
senses.exampleCN: 化石气孔透露出白垩纪的空气。
senses.why: When carbon dioxide is high, plants build fewer openings; the fossil count therefore reads as a climate record.
senses.whyCN: 二氧化碳高时，植物长出的开口更少；化石上的数目于是被读成气候记录。

intro.en: Stomata is the Latinised plural of Greek stoma 'mouth'; botany borrowed the Greek word for the leaf's tiny mouths.
intro.cn: stomata 是希腊 stoma「口」的拉丁化复数；植物学把这个希腊词借来指叶片上的小嘴。

items.en: Greek stoma meant 'mouth, opening', and it also gives stomach, which originally named the gullet.
items.cn: 希腊 stoma 意为「口、开口」，它也是 stomach 的来源，后者原指食道。

items.en: The Greek plural is stomata; English took the plural directly, so stoma and stomata sit side by side.
items.cn: 希腊复数就是 stomata；英语直接借入复数，于是 stoma 与 stomata 并存。

items.en: Nineteenth-century plant anatomy adopted the plural for the pores of the leaf surface, a usage generally accepted by the 1830s.
items.cn: 十九世纪的植物解剖学采用这个复数指叶面的孔，这一用法到 1830 年代一般认为已被接受。

items.en: Zoology kept the older sense of 'mouth' and used the same plural for body openings in invertebrates.
items.cn: 动物学保留了更早的「口」义，并用同一复数指无脊椎动物的体表开口。

items.en: In the twentieth century fossil stomata became a proxy for ancient carbon dioxide levels.
items.cn: 二十世纪，化石气孔成了古代二氧化碳水平的替代指标。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the Greek root is certain, but the date when botany adopted the plural is approximate, and English stress varies between the Latinised and the Greek-style reading.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：希腊词根确定，但植物学采用这个复数的年代只是约数；英语重音在拉丁化读法与希腊式读法之间有差异。

note.en: Group one separates the singular, the variant and a famous same-root word; group two holds other leaf openings.
note.cn: 第一组区分单数、变体与一个同源的著名词；第二组列出叶面上的其他开口。

entries.definition: One opening; the singular is rare in botany because leaves have many.
entries.definitionCN: 一个开口；在植物学中单数少见，因为叶片有很多个。

entries.definition: A variant singular seen in older botany; the plural remains stomata.
entries.definitionCN: 较早植物学中的变体单数；复数仍是 stomata。

entries.definition: From Greek stoma 'mouth' through Latin stomachus; it names the organ, not a leaf pore.
entries.definitionCN: 经拉丁 stomachus 来自希腊 stoma「口」；它指器官，不是叶孔。

entries.definition: The adjective: of or relating to the openings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：与这些开口有关的。

entries.definition: The breathing hole of an insect or a spider; the animal counterpart of a leaf pore.
entries.definitionCN: 昆虫或蜘蛛的呼吸孔；相当于叶孔在动物身上的对应物。

entries.definition: Any small opening in a surface; stomata are one kind of pore.
entries.definitionCN: 表面上任何小开口；气孔是其中一种。

entries.definition: A pore in woody bark for gas exchange; it is not on a leaf.
entries.definitionCN: 木质树皮上供气体交换的孔；不在叶片上。

entries.definition: A pore that releases liquid water, not vapour; it sits at the leaf edge.
entries.definitionCN: 释放液态水而非水汽的孔，位于叶缘。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek root and the real anatomy, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用希腊词根与真实解剖结构，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek stoma 'mouth': the leaf's many tiny mouths.
normal.cn: 希腊 stoma「口」：叶片上许多张小小的嘴。

normal.en: The family: stoma, stomatal, stomatous, stomatitis.
normal.cn: 同族：stoma、stomatal、stomatous、stomatitis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: open stomata, closed stomata, stomata density.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：张开的气孔、闭合的气孔、气孔密度。

normal.en: Two guard cells make one valve, and a leaf holds thousands of valves.
normal.cn: 两个保卫细胞构成一个阀门，一片叶上有成千上万个阀门。

normal.en: The same root also gives stomach, because a mouth is a mouth.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 stomach，因为口就是口。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf surface as a wall of windows that can all be opened at once.
abstract.cn: 想象叶面是一堵可以同时开合的一排窗。

abstract.en: Picture the leaf holding its breath when the soil dries.
abstract.cn: 想象土壤变干时，叶片屏住了呼吸。

abstract.en: Picture a stone-age air sample written in the number of windows.
abstract.cn: 想象一份远古空气样本，写在这些窗口的数目里。

examples.en: The stomata open when the leaf needs to take in air.
examples.cn: 叶片需要吸入空气时，这些气孔就张开。

examples.en: Stomata close when water is scarce.
examples.cn: 缺水时气孔会闭合。

examples.en: Fossil stomata hint at the air of the Cretaceous.
examples.cn: 化石气孔透露出白垩纪的空气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯托马（stoma 口）」的复数——叶片上成排的小嘴，就是气孔

root: 希腊 stoma「口、开口」，复数 stomata，英语直接借入复数。词根清晰；植物学用法的确立年代一般认为在十九世纪三十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses treat the openings as a set, then as a unit, a behaviour, a count, a conductance, a ratio, a pattern, a zoological sense, and finally a fossil climate record.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把这些开口先当作一整套，再当作一个单位、一种行为、一个数目、一种导度、一个比例、一种分布、一个动物学义，最后是一份化石气候记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many small mouths on the leaf that can open and shut together.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶面上许多张能同时开合的小嘴。

branches.en: SET: the plural names the openings as a group.
branches.cn: 集合：复数把这些开口当作一群来命名。

branches.en: UNIT AND VALVE: a gap plus two cells, which can close.
branches.cn: 单位与阀门：一道缝加两个细胞，而它能关闭。

branches.en: COUNT: number per area, then the ratio that normalises size.
branches.cn: 计数：单位面积的数目，再是归一化尺寸的比例。

branches.en: FLOW AND PLACEMENT: conductance measures the flow, placement explains it.
branches.cn: 流动与位置：导度测量流量，分布解释原因。

branches.en: OTHER FIELDS: zoology borrows the mouth, paleobotany borrows the count.
branches.cn: 别的领域：动物学借去「口」，古植物学借去数目。

intro.en: Stomata is a Greek noun and its plural; the family is Greek, with no Latin base word.
intro.cn: stomata 是一个希腊名词及其复数；这个词族属希腊来源，没有拉丁基础词。

latinIntro.en: Greek stoma 'mouth' with the Greek plural -ata builds the word; Latin borrowed it only as a medical and botanical term.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 stoma「口」加希腊复数后缀 -ata 构成这个词；拉丁语只把它作为医学与植物学术语借用。

items.example: It appears before suffixes such as -itis.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 -itis 这类后缀之前。

items.meaningCN: 以 -ma 结尾名词的复数
items.exampleCN: 它把 stoma 变成 stomata。
植物学采用了这个复数。

items.example: The suffix names a field of study.

definition_zh: 气孔的；气孔性的；与叶片气孔有关的
definition_en: relating to stomata, the small openings on a leaf surface
core_image: 所有描述都指向叶面那一排小孔：它们有多大、多少、开还是关
scene: 干旱第三天，田里的玉米叶片先做的一件事是收紧表面的小孔，宁可少长也不肯失水。Stomatal closure is the first defence against drought.
sceneCN: 这里 stomatal 是「气孔关闭的」（第 5 个义项：由气孔限制水汽散失）；句意：关闭气孔是抵御干旱的第一道防线。

pos.zh: 气孔的；与气孔有关的
由气孔引起的；气孔性的

forms.label: 比较级（更受气孔影响的）
最高级（最受气孔影响的）

senses.title: Of the openings
senses.titleCN: 总义：与气孔有关
senses.definition: relating to the openings on a leaf surface
senses.definitionCN: 与叶片表面的气孔有关的
senses.example: Stomatal structure differs between sun and shade leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 阳叶与阴叶的气孔结构不同。
senses.why: The suffix -al simply attaches the noun to another noun: structure, anatomy, question.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 只是把名词挂到另一个名词上：结构、解剖、问题。

senses.title: Movement
senses.titleCN: 运动的：孔口开合的动作
senses.definition: relating to the opening and closing of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔孔口开合有关的
senses.example: Stomatal movement follows the light and the water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔运动随光照与供水而变。
senses.why: The pores move, and the adjective labels the study of that movement rather than the pore itself.
senses.whyCN: 这些孔会动，形容词标的是对这种动作的研究，而不是孔本身。

senses.title: Conductance
senses.titleCN: 导度的：水汽通过的量
senses.definition: relating to the conductance of water vapour and gases through the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与水汽和气体经气孔传导有关的
senses.example: Stomatal conductance fell by half at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午气孔导度降了一半。
senses.why: Physiologists treat the pores as a resistor, and the adjective names the value of that resistance.
senses.whyCN: 生理学家把这些孔当成一个阻力，形容词命名的是那个阻力的值。

senses.title: Density
senses.titleCN: 密度的：单位叶面有多少孔
senses.definition: relating to the number of pores per unit area
senses.definitionCN: 与单位面积气孔数目有关的
senses.example: Stomatal density is a common measure in paleobotany.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔密度是古植物学常用的指标。
senses.why: Counting the pores per area makes them a trait, and the adjective marks that trait.
senses.whyCN: 按面积数孔让它们成为一种性状，形容词标出这一性状。

senses.title: Closure
senses.titleCN: 关闭的：孔口收起来
senses.definition: relating to the closing of the pores, especially under stress
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔关闭（尤指受胁迫时）有关的
senses.example: Stomatal closure is the first defence against drought.
senses.exampleCN: 关闭气孔是抵御干旱的第一道防线。
senses.why: Closing is the active choice of the plant, so the adjective often appears with closure and stress.
senses.whyCN: 关闭是植物主动的选择，所以这个形容词常与关闭和胁迫连用。

senses.title: Limitation
senses.titleCN: 限制的：光合被气孔卡住
senses.definition: relating to the limit that the pores put on photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔对光合作用造成的限制有关的
senses.example: Stomatal limitation explains the midday dip in carbon uptake.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔限制解释了正午碳吸收的下陷。
senses.why: When the pores shut, carbon cannot enter, and the adjective names that bottleneck.
senses.whyCN: 孔一关，碳进不来，形容词命名的是这个瓶颈。

senses.title: Regulation
senses.titleCN: 调节的：植物对孔口的控制
senses.definition: relating to the plant's regulation of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与植物对气孔的调控有关的
senses.example: Stomatal regulation keeps water loss within limits.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔调节把失水控制在限度之内。
senses.why: The adjective marks control rather than structure: who decides when the valve moves.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标的是控制而不是结构：谁决定阀门何时动。

senses.title: Distribution
senses.titleCN: 分布的：上下表面的差别
senses.definition: relating to where the pores are placed on the leaf
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔在叶面上的位置分布有关的
senses.example: Stomatal distribution differs between the two surfaces.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔在两个表面上的分布不同。
senses.why: Placement is a separate fact from number, and the adjective covers it.
senses.whyCN: 位置与数目是两件事，形容词也覆盖了位置。

senses.title: Evolutionary
senses.titleCN: 演化的：气孔在植物史上的出现
senses.definition: relating to the evolutionary origin and change of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔在演化上的起源与变化有关的
senses.example: Stomatal evolution tracks the rise of land plants.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔的演化与陆生植物的兴起同步。
senses.why: The trait has a history, and geology uses the adjective for changes over millions of years.
senses.whyCN: 这一性状有历史，地质学用这个形容词指数百万年尺度的变化。

intro.en: Stomatal is the adjective of stomata, made with the Latin-derived suffix -al on a Greek noun.
intro.cn: stomatal 是 stomata 的形容词，在希腊名词上加了拉丁来源的后缀 -al。

items.en: Greek stoma 'mouth' is the base; the plural stomata entered botany in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 希腊 stoma「口」是基础词；复数 stomata 于十九世纪进入植物学。

items.en: The suffix -al, from Latin -alis, means 'relating to' and is added to nouns of any origin.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 来自拉丁 -alis，意为「与……有关的」，可加在任何来源的名词上。

items.en: Plant anatomists needed an adjective for pore structure, movement and density, and stomatal supplied all three.
items.cn: 植物解剖学家需要一个形容词来指孔的结构、运动与密度，stomatal 一次满足了这三样。

items.en: Twentieth-century physiology fixed phrases such as stomatal conductance and stomatal limitation.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生理学固定了 stomatal conductance、stomatal limitation 这类短语。

items.en: The same adjective now appears in studies that read ancient carbon dioxide from fossil pore counts.
items.cn: 同一个形容词现在也出现在从化石孔数读出古代二氧化碳的研究里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the elements are certain, but the first printed use of the adjective is undated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：成分确定，但这个形容词首次印刷使用的年份没有记载。

note.en: Group one separates the noun family from look-alikes; group two holds adjectives for nearby leaf surfaces and openings.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词词族与形近词；第二组列出描述邻近叶面与开口的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural noun itself; the adjective adds -al and shifts the final syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 复数名词本身；形容词加 -al，并把末音节改掉。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning 'having pores'; stomatal is the usual modern form for 'relating to pores'.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的形容词，意为「有孔的」；现代常用 stomatal 表示「与孔有关的」。

entries.definition: The organ, from the same Greek word for 'mouth'; the meaning is medical, not botanical.
entries.definitionCN: 器官，来自同一个希腊词「口」；意义属医学，不属植物学。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the mouth; the suffix -itis marks disease.
entries.definitionCN: 口腔炎症；后缀 -itis 标出疾病。

entries.definition: Relating to the outer cell layer that carries the pores.
entries.definitionCN: 与承载气孔的外层细胞有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to the waxy covering that limits water loss around the pores.
entries.definitionCN: 与气孔周围限制失水的蜡质层有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to the pores in bark, the woody counterpart of leaf pores.
entries.definitionCN: 与树皮上的孔有关，是叶孔在木质部分的对应物。

entries.definition: Relating to pores that release liquid water rather than vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 与释放液态水而非水汽的孔有关的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实后缀与真实搭配，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: stomata + -al: 'relating to the leaf's small mouths'.
normal.cn: stomata 加 -al：「与叶片小嘴有关的」。

normal.en: The family: stoma, stomata, stomatous, stomatitis.
normal.cn: 同族：stoma、stomata、stomatous、stomatitis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: stomatal closure, stomatal conductance, stomatal density.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：气孔关闭、气孔导度、气孔密度。

normal.en: Three questions the adjective answers: how many, how open, how much flows.
normal.cn: 这个形容词回答三个问题：有多少、开多大、通过多少。

normal.en: Closure, limitation and regulation are the stress words that go with it.
normal.cn: 关闭、限制、调节是常与它连用的胁迫词。

abstract.en: Picture a valve chart on the wall of a greenhouse, with every valve drawn small.
abstract.cn: 想象温室墙上挂着一张阀门图，每个阀门都画得很小。

abstract.en: Picture a plant choosing to shut its windows rather than lose its water.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物选择关上窗户，而不是失水。

abstract.en: Picture a number written on a leaf that says how tightly the leaf is holding its breath.
abstract.cn: 想象叶片上写着一个数，说明它屏气屏得多紧。

examples.en: Stomatal closure is the first defence against drought.
examples.cn: 关闭气孔是抵御干旱的第一道防线。

examples.en: Stomatal conductance fell by half at noon.
examples.cn: 正午气孔导度降了一半。

examples.en: Stomatal density is a common measure in paleobotany.
examples.cn: 气孔密度是古植物学常用的指标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「气孔（stomata）＋的（-al）」——凡指叶面小孔的数目、开合与导度

root: 希腊 stoma「口」的复数 stomata 加拉丁来源的形容词后缀 -al（来自 -alis，「与……有关的」）。词根清晰，形容词首见年代无确切记载。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all point at the same pores from different angles: structure, movement, conductance, density, closure, limitation, regulation, placement, and evolutionary history.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从不同角度指向同一批小孔：结构、运动、导度、密度、关闭、限制、调节、位置，以及演化史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every statement about a leaf's small valves, whether of size, number or state.
core.cn: 核心意象：关于叶片那些小阀门的一切陈述，无论讲大小、数目还是状态。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTE: the adjective first just says 'of the pores'.
branches.cn: 属性：这个形容词最初只说「与孔有关的」。

branches.en: CONTROL: movement and regulation describe what the plant decides.
branches.cn: 控制：运动与调节描述植物所作的决定。

branches.en: FLOW: conductance measures it, limitation names where it blocks.
branches.cn: 流动：导度测量它，限制命名它卡住的地方。

branches.en: COUNT AND PLACE: how many per area, and where they sit.
branches.cn: 数目与位置：单位面积多少，以及它们待在哪。

branches.en: STRESS AND TIME: closure under drought, evolution over ages.
branches.cn: 胁迫与时间：干旱下关闭，漫长年代里的演化。

intro.en: Stomatal is a Greek noun plus the Latin-derived suffix -al; the suffix is Latin, the base is Greek.
intro.cn: stomatal 是希腊名词加拉丁来源的后缀 -al；后缀属拉丁，基础词属希腊。

latinIntro.en: Greek stoma 'mouth' supplies the base; Latin -alis supplies the adjective ending; the combination is modern scientific English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 stoma「口」提供基础；拉丁 -alis 提供形容词词尾；组合发生在现代科学英语里。

items.example: It attaches to nouns of any origin.
items.exampleCN: 它可加在任何来源的名词上。

items.example: An older synonym of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 该形容词较早的同义词。

items.example: The medical branch of the family.

definition_zh: 蒸腾作用；植物体内水分经气孔散失到空气的过程
definition_en: the loss of water vapour from plants, mainly through the stomata
core_image: 根吸上来的水走完整株植物，最后从叶面变成水汽散进空气
scene: 正午的玉米地叶片卷起，根吸上来的水大部分并没有留在植株里。Most of that water leaves the field by transpiration.
sceneCN: 这里 transpiration 指「植物经气孔散失水汽的过程」（第 1 个义项：作为整株植物的失水过程）；句意：那些水大部分以蒸腾作用离开了这块田。

pos.zh: 蒸腾作用（植物失水，不可数）
散发；蒸发（一般意义的水汽散出）

senses.title: Water loss from plants
senses.titleCN: 植物失水：水从叶面变成水汽
senses.definition: the loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through its stomata
senses.definitionCN: 植物主要经气孔散失水汽的过程
senses.example: Most of that water leaves the field by transpiration.
senses.exampleCN: 那些水大部分以蒸腾作用离开了这块田。
senses.why: The plant is a wick: water enters at the roots, moves up, and leaves as vapour at the leaves.
senses.whyCN: 植物就是一根烛芯：水从根进、往上走，最后在叶片以水汽离开。

senses.title: The pull
senses.titleCN: 蒸腾拉力：水柱被向上拽
senses.definition: the tension that the loss of vapour creates, drawing water up the plant
senses.definitionCN: 水汽散失造成的拉力，把水沿植物体向上拉
senses.example: Transpiration pull lifts water to the tallest leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾拉力把水送到最高的叶片。
senses.why: Every litre that leaves the leaf pulls another litre up behind it, so loss and lift are one mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 每从叶片走掉一升水，就往上拽进另一升，于是失水与提升是同一套机制。

senses.title: Rate
senses.titleCN: 速率：单位时间失去多少水
senses.definition: the measured rate at which a plant loses water vapour
senses.definitionCN: 单位时间内散失水汽的速率
senses.example: They measured transpiration with a potometer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用蒸腾计测蒸腾速率。
senses.why: Once the process is named, instruments can give it a number, and the word comes to mean that number.
senses.whyCN: 过程一旦有了名字，仪器就能给它一个数，这个词也随之指那个数。

senses.title: Cooling
senses.titleCN: 降温：失水带走热量
senses.definition: the cooling of a leaf that the evaporation of water produces
senses.definitionCN: 水分蒸发给叶片带来的降温
senses.example: Transpiration keeps the leaf below air temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾让叶温低于气温。
senses.why: Evaporation takes heat with it, so the same loss that costs water also saves the leaf from overheating.
senses.whyCN: 蒸发会带走热量，于是这份失水在耗水的同时，也让叶片免于过热。

senses.title: Stomatal control
senses.titleCN: 气孔调控：开合决定失水快慢
senses.definition: the regulation of water loss by the opening and closing of the stomata
senses.definitionCN: 气孔开合对失水快慢的调控
senses.example: Transpiration stops when the stomata close at midday.
senses.exampleCN: 正午气孔关闭时，蒸腾就停止了。
senses.why: The pores are the tap, and the word covers whatever flow the tap allows.
senses.whyCN: 气孔是龙头，这个词覆盖龙头允许的那股流量。

senses.title: Water-use ratio
senses.titleCN: 蒸腾比：造一克干物质要用多少水
senses.definition: the ratio of water lost to dry matter gained
senses.definitionCN: 失水量与所得干物质之比
senses.example: A low transpiration ratio marks a thrifty crop.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾比低说明这种作物省水。
senses.why: Farmers compare outputs, so the process becomes a ratio of cost to yield.
senses.whyCN: 农人要比较产出，于是这个过程变成一个成本与产量的比值。

senses.title: General vapor release
senses.titleCN: 一般散发：任何表面散出水汽
senses.definition: the release of water vapour from any surface, not only from plants
senses.definitionCN: 任何表面散出水汽，不限于植物
senses.example: Transpiration from the wet soil continued all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 湿土散出的水汽持续了一下午。
senses.why: The word began as a general term for giving off vapour, and the botanical sense narrowed one part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初泛指散出水汽，植物义只是把其中一部分收窄了。

senses.title: Sweat and exhalation
senses.titleCN: 人体散发：出汗与呼出水汽
senses.definition: the giving off of moisture through the skin or the breath, an older medical use
senses.definitionCN: 经皮肤或呼吸散出水分，属较早的医学用法
senses.example: Old medical texts speak of transpiration through the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的医学文献说到经皮肤的散发。
senses.why: Before it belonged to botany, the word described the body's own invisible moisture, and medicine kept that sense.
senses.whyCN: 在归植物学之前，这个词描述身体自己看不见的水分，医学保留了这层意思。

senses.title: Vapour flux in the water cycle
senses.titleCN: 水汽通量：区域尺度上的失水
senses.definition: the flux of water vapour from a region, summed over its vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域植被总体散出的水汽通量
senses.example: Transpiration returns a large share of rainfall to the air.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾把降水的很大一部分送回空中。
senses.why: Scale the wick from one plant to a catchment and the word becomes a term in the water budget.
senses.whyCN: 把这根烛芯从一株植物放大到一个集水区，这个词就成了水量收支里的一个项。

intro.en: Transpiration joins Latin trans- 'across' to spirare 'to breathe', literally 'a breathing through'.
intro.cn: transpiration 把拉丁 trans-「穿过」与 spirare「呼吸」连起来，字面是「透过去呼吸」。

items.en: Latin spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow', and it also gives spirit, inspire and expire.
items.cn: 拉丁 spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」，它也是 spirit、inspire、expire 的来源。

items.en: Transpirare meant 'to breathe through, to emit vapour', built with the prefix trans- 'across, through'.
items.cn: transpirare 意为「透过去呼吸、散出水汽」，由前缀 trans-「穿过」构成。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the seventeenth century for the giving off of invisible moisture, including from the body.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，指散出看不见的水分，包括身体散出的。

items.en: Nineteenth-century plant physiology narrowed the word to water loss through the stomata, the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 十九世纪的植物生理学把这个词收窄为经气孔失水，这一义项如今占主导。

items.en: Twentieth-century hydrology extended it again, to vapour fluxes summed over whole regions.
items.cn: 二十世纪的水文学又把它扩展为整个区域的水汽通量。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the Latin roots are certain, but the first English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁词根确定，但英语首次使用的年代只有约数。

note.en: Group one separates the same-root breathing words from the one that means sweat; group two holds the water-loss terms it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组区分同源的「呼吸」词与表示出汗的那个词；第二组列出常被混淆的失水术语。

entries.definition: The verb: to give off vapour, and informally to become known.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：散出水汽；口语里也指事情逐渐为人所知。

entries.definition: Per- 'through' plus spirare: sweat, the body's own moisture.
entries.definitionCN: per-「穿过」加 spirare：汗，身体自己的水分。

entries.definition: Re- plus spirare: breathing and the release of energy from sugar.
entries.definitionCN: re- 加 spirare：呼吸，以及从糖中释放能量。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: drawing breath, and the figurative breath of an idea.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 spirare：吸气，以及想法带来的那口气。

entries.definition: Water turning to vapour from any surface; transpiration is its living-plant case.
entries.definitionCN: 水从任何表面变成水汽；蒸腾是它在活植物身上的情形。

entries.definition: The release of liquid water drops at leaf edges, not vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 叶缘释放液态水滴，不是水汽。

entries.definition: The slow release of sap or fluid from a wound or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 汁液或液体从伤口或表面缓慢渗出。

entries.definition: Evaporation from soil plus transpiration from plants, added together.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾相加的总量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin pieces and the real physiology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用拉丁部件与真实生理过程，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: trans- 'through' + spirare 'to breathe': breathing through the leaf.
normal.cn: trans-「穿过」加 spirare「呼吸」：透过叶片呼吸。

normal.en: The family: transpire, transpiratory, evapotranspiration, perspiration.
normal.cn: 同族：transpire、transpiratory、evapotranspiration、perspiration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rate of transpiration, transpiration stream, transpiration pull.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：蒸腾速率、蒸腾流、蒸腾拉力。

normal.en: One wick, two jobs: it lifts water and it cools the leaf.
normal.cn: 一根烛芯，两件活：把水提上去，把叶子降温。

normal.en: Compare with perspiration: one is the plant's breath, one is the body's sweat.
normal.cn: 与 perspiration 对照：一个是植物的呼吸，一个是身体的汗。

abstract.en: Picture a tall tree as a straw that the air is slowly drinking from.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵高树是一根被空气慢慢吸饮的吸管。

abstract.en: Picture a field exhaling water into the sky all afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田整个下午都在向天空呼出水汽。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where the water lost and the crop gained are written in one ratio.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，把失去的水与得到的作物写成一个比值。

examples.en: Most of that water leaves the field by transpiration.
examples.cn: 那些水大部分以蒸腾作用离开了这块田。

examples.en: Transpiration pull lifts water to the tallest leaves.
examples.cn: 蒸腾拉力把水送到最高的叶片。

examples.en: Transpiration stops when the stomata close at midday.
examples.cn: 正午气孔关闭时，蒸腾就停止了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿过（trans）＋呼吸（spir）」——植物透过叶片向外呼气，把水汽送走

root: 拉丁 trans-「穿过」＋ spirare「呼吸」→ transpirare「透过去呼吸、散出水汽」。词根清晰；英语首见年代只有约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one current: water leaves the leaf, pulls more up behind it, is measured, cools the leaf, is controlled by the pores, becomes a farming ratio, widens to any surface, widens further to the body, and finally to a region's water budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一股水流展开：水离开叶片、把后面的水往上拽、被测量、给叶片降温、受气孔控制、变成农业比值，再扩到任何表面、扩到身体，最后扩到一个区域的水量收支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wick that carries water from the root to the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根把水从根送到空气里的烛芯。

branches.en: LOSS: the word first names the water leaving the plant.
branches.cn: 失去：这个词首先命名离开植物的水。

branches.en: TWO EFFECTS: the same loss lifts water and takes heat away.
branches.cn: 两个效果：同一份失水既提水又带走热。

branches.en: NUMBERS: rate and ratio turn the process into a quantity.
branches.cn: 数字：速率与比值把过程变成量。

branches.en: VALVE: the pores decide how fast the loss runs.
branches.cn: 阀门：气孔决定失水跑多快。

branches.en: WIDER: any surface, the body, a whole catchment.
branches.cn: 更广：任何表面、身体、整个集水区。

intro.en: Transpiration is Latin throughout: a Latin prefix, a Latin verb stem, and a Latin noun suffix.
intro.cn: transpiration 全部来自拉丁语：拉丁前缀、拉丁动词词干、拉丁名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans- 'through' and spirare 'to breathe' give transpirare; -ation, from -atio, names the action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trans-「穿过」与 spirare「呼吸」给出 transpirare；-ation 来自 -atio，命名动作或结果。

items.example: It also appears in transport and translate.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 transport 与 translate 里。

items.example: The bare stem carries the breath.
It makes a noun of the act.
The English noun dates from the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词始于十七世纪。

items.example: The verb is the base of the noun.
The compound is a modern hydrology term.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是现代水文学术语。
